#2027. Michael Carrick clashes with Sky Sports reporter in spiky interview over his future: Man United boss expects to continue despite club being in relegation zone after 4-4 draw with Villa

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 15:17 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 16:08 EST, 8 November 2026

Michael Carrick insists he won't quit as Manchester United boss despite having to see his team spend the international break in the relegation zone.

United staged another incredible fightback to snatch a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford after trailing by two goals heading into injury-time.

But it wasn't enough to spare the club from the humiliation of being in the bottom three for the next two weeks – the longest United have spent there since 1986.

The manner of the performance and result will only heap further pressure on Carrick and when the future of his own position was put to him by Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davison, the United boss took exception to the question in a spiky interview.

'What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? You've been asked time and again about your future? I know you have said that you walking away was the best for the club, you'd probably do it,' Davison asked Carrick.

'It's not going to happen, no,' Carrick replied.

"That's not going to happen" 🗣️Michael Carrick responds to the notion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach 🔴 pic.twitter.com/q1fBKSXL7l

Michael Carrick was involved in a spiky interview with Sky Sports about his Man United future

Patrick Dorgu (centre) scored a late equaliser as troubled Man United drew 4-4 vs Aston Villa

Despite Sunday's draw, Carrick's position as United head coach looks increasingly doubtful

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week. They conceded twice at the start of each half against Villa, and have now let in 30 goals in all competitions – the joint highest in Europe's top five leagues.

'We're making it hard for ourselves. Mistakes that the boys know shouldn't happen,' added Carrick. 'Two goals again put us on the back foot. We beat ourselves a little bit with the goals that we're giving away in tight clusters. It's hard enough anyway, but we're making it a lot more difficult than it should be.

'I thought we were the better team. We never gave up and never stopped believing. I'm disappointed that we still haven't won the game, to be truthful.'

The United fans kept behind Carrick and his team while once again targeting the club's owners, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

However, there were loud cheers when Diogo Dalot was replaced in the 66th minute. It was reminiscent of the treatment of Joshua Zirkzee by the home supporters when he was substituted against Newcastle in December 2024, and the Dutchman made a point of giving Dalot a reassuring hug in the dugout.

'We've got to be careful with that,' said Carrick. 'I understand the frustration and the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it. We're all frustrated, we're all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

'Diogo gives absolutely everything. He's played in different positions, he's played left-back, he's played really well at times.

'He gave a penalty away today, he knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better. He's made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he's giving everything.'

Dalot's replacement Patrick Dorgu led the fightback, five days after United had recovered from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2, as he crossed for Zirkzee to pull a goal back and then headed the equaliser in the 96th minute.

'I don't feel happy,' said Dorgu. 'We are in a bad situation and we need to fight together to get out of it. A draw is better than a loss, but everyone needs to look at themselves and ask if they are doing enough. We need to fight for the manager, for the club and get out of this together.

'Of course, it hurts (to be in relegation zone). There are a lot of games and we need everyone to come back sharp from international break and start getting wins.'

Teammate Matheus Cunha added: 'We are so disappointed. Before anything else we need to look inside to us – the players, the staff. It's a huge club and to feel something like this (being in the relegation zone) is not normal.'

It's not the first time Carrick has engaged in an interesting post-match interview this season. In August, he snapped at a reporter's 'ridiculous' opening question after Manchester United's shock defeat at Hull City on the opening day of the season.

Carrick was affronted when asked if his players had lost against the newly promoted club due to a lack of 'passion'.

United's Premier League season got off to a nightmare start as goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy - both stemming from set-pieces - put them to the sword in Yorkshire.

Carrick was interviewed afterwards by Viaplay broadcaster Jan Age Fjortoft, the Norwegian who played for Swindon, Middlesbrough, Sheffield United and Barnsley in the 1990s.

“Come on, that’s ridiculous.”Michael Carrick wasn’t happy when asked if there was a lack of passion from #mufc in their first half vs Hull.via @ViaplayFotball pic.twitter.com/zyca5r5iSr

In August, Carrick said it was 'ridiculous' to suggest United lacked passion after losing to Hull

He was vexed by the question posed by Viaplay reporter and former play Jan Age Fjortoft

'Would you accept that there was a lack of passion in the first half?' asked Fjortoft.

'Oh come on, that's ridiculous,' Carrick hit back.

'That's not how you would assess it?' asked Fjortoft.

Carrick replied: 'Come on, you played football, you understand, that's a ridiculous thing to say. Just because you got beat doesn't mean you don't care about it.'

Fjortoft said: 'I'm not saying that you didn't care about it. If you look at it, they came with passion, that's what I mean. I understand that you care about it, but would you accept that they took you on that front, so to say?'

'No, no. Their two goals came from set plays. Other than that, we had opportunities,' Carrick said. 'That was where the game was. I don't think it was passion or anything to do with that. I think it was just their moment that made the difference in the game.'

Fjortoft said: 'Is it these duels? Is that what you mean? That these two duels were the goals? Because they had chances. There were consequences there from the game that you could see that they would get at you.'

'It's a game of football, it's a Premier League game,' Carrick replied.

'It's their first game at home, and we've seen it many times before. You know, I said it before the game because it was always going to be a tough game.

'And set-plays, yeah, that's it. We've been decent over a period of time at dealing with them, and today we didn't.

'We can look into that, we can dissect it. We certainly won't get carried away with the positives or the negatives. We never do. So I think we can stay calm and understand what we need to get better at.'

After the international break though United face the ultimate litmus test when they travel to bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on November 22.

John Aldridge has questioned why Liverpool weren’t more assertive in pulling Dominik Szoboszlai out of national team duty when he’s currently nursing a minor injury.

The midfielder sprained his ankle in the 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace on Sunday, with Andoni Iraola uncertain after the game as to whether or not the 26-year-old would join up with his country during this international window.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Hungarian FA said that a decision on the player’s participation against Georgia and Northern Ireland over the next week will be deferred until the ‘last minute’ as his fitness continues to be assessed.

In his latest column for the Liverpool Echo, Aldridge voiced his belief that Liverpool should’ve done more to prevent Szoboszlai from playing for Hungary in the coming days when he’s clearly not fully fit.

The former Reds striker wrote: ‘I know Virgil van Dijk has pulled out of the Netherlands squad because of a little niggle, but Dominik Szoboszlai has stayed with Hungary despite injuring his knee against Palace.

‘Any other club would pull them out of international duty. Manchester United, Arsenal, Man City – they’d all pull them. We’ve seen it before. Any doubt and that’s it, decision made, you’re not playing. I don’t understand why we don’t throw our weight around like that.

‘I understand players want to play for their country. I was the same with Ireland. I would answer call-ups even when I was injured. I get what it means and how much it means to players, but any other club would just pull them. That’s not happened here, I don’t know why. Hopefully that just means it’s not that serious.

‘It still sounds like they’re taking a risk. If he stays with Hungary and plays, we’ve just got to hope the decision doesn’t backfire and come back to hurt Liverpool.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

As Szoboszlai is contracted to Liverpool, the Merseyside club could’ve blocked him from representing his country during this international window because of his knee injury.

However, it’d appear to be a case of the player wanting to at least link up with the Hungary camp and try to prove his fitness, and Anfield chiefs green-lighting that action out of respect for the 26-year-old and not wanting to antagonise him by forbidding him to travel.

The grey area over the midfielder potentially being fit enough to play but not certain of doing so has presented a tricky dilemma, as much as Iraola would no doubt have preferred for our number 8 to swerve national team duty and prioritise his club instead.

With Hungary not playing until Saturday, that does give Szoboszlai a bit of time to recover from the knee issue he incurred at Selhurst Park, and we’d like to think that Marco Rossi wouldn’t risk fielding him against Georgia unless he’s definitely OK to feature.

While a swift return to action for the 26-year-old would obviously be a good thing, we just hope it doesn’t come at the expense of his involvement for Liverpool in the coming weeks, especially with a hectic run of 11 matches in 40 days before the end of December.

#2024. Premier League KMI panel issues emphatic verdict on Alexander Isak penalty decision v Arsenal

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has concluded that Liverpool should’ve had a penalty awarded for an offence by Jurrien Timber on Alexander Isak in their defeat to Arsenal earlier this month.

Five minutes after Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game at Anfield, the Swedish striker had his shirt pulled in the box by the Gunners defender, but neither on-field referee Andy Madley nor Stuart Attwell on VAR felt compelled to award a spot kick despite the transgression being clear.

The Reds’ head coach Andoni Iraola went as far as claiming that a penalty would’ve been awarded had our number 9 gone to ground instead of staying on his feet when his jersey was grabbed.

On Wednesday, the Premier League published the findings of several incidents reviewed by the KMI Panel, including the one involving Isak and Timber on 1 November.

Their verdict reads (via premierleague.com): ‘The panel felt that a penalty should have been awarded for a holding action by Timber on Isak, 4:1. One panellist considered the short-lived holding to lack clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress.

‘The majority also felt that VAR should have intervened to recommend an on-field review, 3:2, on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error. Two panellists considered that the subjectivity in assessing impact meant this did not meet the high threshold for VAR intervention.’

The KMI Panel concluded: ‘In this instance the panel deemed that Timber’s challenge on Isak met the threshold for a holding offence and should have resulted in a penalty kick, both on-field and through VAR intervention.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

How nice of the KMI Panel to come back and tell us what was so damn obvious at the time of the incident – or at least obvious to anyone not named Andy Madley or Stuart Attwell, or whichever member of the panel felt that the right decision was made on the day.

How that individual concluded that Timber’s actions lacked ‘clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress’ is baffling – the Liverpool striker would surely have gotten on the end of Bradley Barcola’s cross had his shirt not been so blatantly pulled.

The panel’s verdict today won’t come as much consolation to anyone involved with the Reds, who were deprived of a legitimate penalty which – if converted – could’ve significantly altered the course of a match that they lost 1-0.

It’s not much good being told in retrospect that the officials got it wrong; these are clear decisions that professional referees should be capable of getting correct at the time, especially when they have the fallback option of VAR.

We get that many incidents are subjective and that consensus will never be achieved when it comes to refereeing in the Premier League, but there’s simply no excuse for botching calls like the Timber/Isak incident 10 days ago.

#2022. Astonishing moment manager HEADBUTTS opposition player and is sent off, sparking mass brawl as FA Cup first round clash descends into chaos

By JAMES DUTTON, DEPUTY SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and WILL GOVE

Published: 16:39 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 16:41 EST, 8 November 2026

Oldham boss Micky Mellon was sent off for headbutting Sheffield Wednesday midfielder Callum Slattery as their FA Cup first round clash descended into a mass brawl at Boundary Park.

League Two Oldham pulled off a shock over their League One opponents, but the result was overshadowed by the altercation which occurred six minutes from the end of normal time.

The former Blackpool and Burnley midfielder appeared to grab Slattery by the back of the neck and pulled him closer to his face, before pushing his head into the rival player’s face and knocking him over.

The touchline soon descended into chaos with players and staff from both teams grappling with each other in a farcical melee.

Eventually the two warring sides were separated giving referee Martin Woods the opportunity to approach Mellon and present him with a thoroughly deserved red card.

Oldham, now with their manager in the stands, played on and incredibly nicked a 110th minute winner through Will Sutton.

Oldham Athletic manager Micky Mellon is shown a red card for moving his head towards Wednesday's Callum Slattery 🟥📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/5QMxgLt0dO

Oldham manager Micky Mellon was sent off for an astonishing headbutt on Sheffield Wednesday midfielder Callum Slattery

The scene soon descended into chaos as both players and staff from both sides entered the melee

Eventually Mellon was shown a red card and will serve a three match touchline ban

Wednesday piled on the pressure in the final minutes desperately trying to find an equaliser but to no avail as Oldham held on and advanced into the next round.

Mellon, however, will now have to serve a three-match touchline ban meaning he will miss his side's next appearance in this year's FA Cup.

Calum Kavanagh had put Oldham ahead in the 66th minute with a fierce drive after Mike Fondop headed on Noah Chilvers’ right-wing cross – his sixth goal of the season.

Wednesday equalised ten minutes later through former Oldham forward Davis Keillor-Dunn.

Elsewhere in the FA Cup on Sunday, seventh-tier Wimborne Town stunned League Two Crawley 2-0 to reach the second round for the first time in their history.

The Dorset part-timers of the Southern League Premier Division South took the lead through Yang Seung-woo’s stunning strike after nine minutes, with Cameron Munn deflecting in Jackson King’s shot 11 minutes from time to seal the upset.

Stockport survived a scare to beat Cray Wanderers of the Isthmian League Premier Division 3-2.

The League One high-flyers were facing a shock exit when they fell two goals behind in the first half, a situation not helped by a red card for goalkeeper Luca Ashby-Hammond for a foul outside the box.

From the free-kick, defender Alex Hernandez found the top corner to make it 2-0, but Stockport staged a late fightback, Kyle Wootton and, in added time, Mikael Mandron scoring to take the tie to extra time before Lewis Fiorini’s penalty won it.

Eighth-tier Stafford Rangers also led EFL opposition 2-0 before bowing out, Grimsby finding themselves facing an embarrassing exit against a team four divisions lower before hitting back to make it 3-3 after extra time, eventually going through on penalties.

“I shouldn’t judge him: he’s younger than me, but he has a lot more experience than me. I learn from him. We study him, we watch him. He plays with a system I really like.

#2020. ‘Right now…’ – Liverpool-linked Premier League star makes his plans clear amid transfer rumours

One Premier League player who’s reportedly being targeted by Liverpool has issued a reponse to the transfer speculation surrounding him.

Earlier this week, TEAMtalk claimed that Anfield chiefs are eyeing Bart Verbruggen as a potential long-term successor to Alisson Becker, who’s now 34 and – as it stands – will be out of contract in seven months’ time.

The Brighton goalkeeper was reportedly among a shortlist of candidates being considered by the Reds prior to the summer transfer window, with the Merseysiders eventually agreeing a deal to sign Lucca Brughmans, who’ll join from Genk next summer.

Verbruggen – who’s currently with the Netherlands squad for their concluding UEFA Nations League fixtures – has insisted that despite the rumoured interest from Liverpool, he’s more than happy with the Seagulls, who currently sit second in the Premier League.

The 24-year-old said (via NOS): “Right now we’re doing really well at Brighton, so it would be a real shame to ruin that by living in the future. I really try to stay in the moment, to focus on what is currently going on. I enjoy that, and that is also how I perform best.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Brighton’s magnificent season so far has been underpinned by the excellence of the man between the sticks, who’s kept seven clean sheets in 10 league games and conceded just three times in eight top-flight matches since a 4-3 defeat at Chelsea in August (Transfermarkt).

Figures from Fotmob show that he’s prevented 4.39 xG worth of goals for his team, more than anyone else in the Premier League, and he put in a heroic display in the Seagulls’ recent win at Manchester City as he recorded no fewer than seven saves (Sky Sports).

Those performance levels would indicate that he’d be an ideal successor to Alisson, although there’s been renewed hope in recent days that Liverpool’s number 1 could extend his contract for another year or two, with his agent currently in talks with the club to that effect.

Giorgi Mamardashvili was signed with the intention of succeeding the Brazilian eventually, although the 26-year-old hasn’t always convinced during his time with the Reds so far, and Brughmans will add to the queue once he joins ahead of next season.

Right now there wouldn’t seem to be any urgent need for LFC to move heaven and earth to sign Verbruggen, but if circumstances were to change regarding their current goalkeeping options, it could be worth keeping a hand in should the opportunity arise to move for the Brighton stopper.

#2018. Joe Hart pinpoints ‘unbelievable’ Alisson Becker trait which makes him ‘one of the best’

Joe Hart has proclaimed that Alisson Becker will ‘forever be regarded as one of the best’ goalkeepers to have graced the Premier League.

Liverpool’s number 1 has been rightly acknowledged as one of the foremost players in his position in world football since his move to Anfield in 2018 and has been pivotal towards the trophies won by the Reds in that time.

He produced one of his greatest LFC performances in the victory at Crystal Palace last weekend, with his tally of six saves including a world-class reaction stop from Daichi Kamada which left the Eagles attacker astounded.

In an interview with The Athletic, Hart lavished praise on Alisson for the consistency he’s shown throughout his time in England, and especially his prowess in one-on-saves.

The ex-Manchester City stopper said of the 34-year-old: “One of the best to do it in the Premier League. What I love is his simplicity. He’s not necessarily eye-catching in the way he moves, but it’s the way he deals with everything.

“He makes massive saves. His one-on-one technique is unbelievable, and he has made it his own. He very rarely gets beaten one-on-one, which in this Premier League is incredible because you’re up against some of the best strikers in the world.

“He’s struggled a bit with injuries lately, but I think he’ll forever be regarded as one of the best to play the position.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Last weekend, Alisson produced a perfect example of the one-on-one ability that Hart pinpointed by thwarting Yeremy Pino when the Crystal Palace forward was through on goal, a significant intervention at a time that Liverpool were 2-0 up.

When it comes to ‘massive saves’, it mightn’t quite be in the same category as his legendary stoppage-time heroics against Napoli in December 2018 when our Champions League campaign was in the balance, but it showed that the 34-year-old remains a world-class goalkeeper.

His outstanding display at Selhurst Park came after a couple of costly misjudgements in defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, which shows the Brazilian’s strength of character to put those unfortunate moments behind him and come up trumps for his team.

Alisson’s agent Ze Maria revealed in recent days that talks have begun over a prospective contract renewal at Liverpool, with the Reds’ number 1 having said after the win at Palace that he’d like to stay at Anfield beyond the expiry of his current deal next summer.

More heroics like those he produced in south London four days ago, and an extension to his existing terms should be a no-brainer for sporting director Julian Ward.

#2017. HEARTS 2 FALKIRK 5: Wouter Vrancken slams 'childish' Hearts as five-star Bairns toy with injury-hit capital men at Tynecastle

Published: 16:57 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 17:00 EST, 8 November 2026

Wouter Vrancken condemned a ‘ridiculous’ first-half display from his sorry Hearts side as their 18-month unbeaten home record in the Premiership was ripped apart by ruthless Falkirk.

The beleaguered Tynecastle side, who went into the game without 11 players through injury following a gruelling run of fixtures, endured a dismal afternoon as the Bairns raced into a 4-0 half-time lead on their way to a fifth Premiership win in a row.

Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double had the visitors 5-0 up within 47 minutes before Hearts reduced the deficit through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle since April 2025 for the Gorgie men, who have now won just two of their last 11 matches in all competitions.

‘This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure,’ said Vrancken. ‘Always doubting, always doing things half-half, in possession, out of possession, everything, and such easy goals again.

‘When you give those easy goals, then you cannot win a game. It’s childish goals and cannot happen on this level. Those simple things, they are the basics actually in these situations.

American striker Jacob Murrell races off to celebrate his side's fifth goal on a day to remember

‘It’s crazy, crazy, and everybody — me, staff, players — have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous.’

To exacerbate their grim predicament, Hearts lost yet another senior player as defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

‘This also makes me a bit angry, because now we lose Mal again,’ said Vrancken. ‘Hopefully it’s not too bad, but still we had to replace him there, because he was one of the guys who was good in the game and in the last games actually he had a really consistent, good level.’

Hearts were leapfrogged into third place by Falkirk, who secured five consecutive top-flight victories for the first time in 31 years.

‘I’ve never been 5-0 up here before,’ said Bairns manager John McGlynn. ‘First half we were outstanding. A great start to the game for us to get the goal so early.

‘We got ourselves 4-0 up at half-time, which is dreamland. Hearts had a lot of the ball and dominated the second period, but we’re taking 5-2 every day of the week, make no mistake about it.’

Wouter Vrancken has been beset by injury concerns but he was in no mood for excuses

The Bairns seized the lead in the fourth minute. After Murrell’s close-range effort from Scott Tanser’s cross was brilliantly saved by Beau Reus, Barbrook reacted quickest to drill home a low, angled finish from eight yards out.

Falkirk doubled their lead in the 17th minute after the hosts were caught wide open on the counter-attack. Yan Dhanda’s shot from distance was charged down, allowing the Bairns to break swiftly, with Brad Spencer weighting his pass perfectly for Eames who fired past the exposed Reus.

Braga thought he had pulled one back for Hearts in the 20th minute, but it was ruled out for handball.

Falkirk took full advantage of this reprieve by adding a third in the 33rd minute as Murrell peeled off Fagan-Walcott at the back post to nod home Deniss Melniks’ cross from the right.

The visitors struck again in first-half stoppage-time as Henderson curled high past Reus after Tanser’s corner broke to him just inside the box.

Within two minutes of the restart Falkirk notched again as Murrell fired home after being set up by Ethan Ross.

Former Hearts boss John McGlynn led his side to a quite remarkable fifth consecutive win

Hearts got off the mark when Guendouz drilled in his first goal for the club from just inside the box in the 50th minute. Braga then tucked away a penalty in the 74th minute after Guendouz was tripped by Lewis Neilson, but it was far too little, far too late.

McGlynn added: ‘We had to smell blood and we had to go for it and that’s exactly what happened. Our play was outstanding in the first half. We won every duel, we won everything all over the park.

‘Winning five on the trot has not been done since 1995, Jim Jefferies’ team, so I’m delighted for everyone at the football club that we’ve managed to equal that record.’

#2015. Liverpool could replicate Jeremy Jacquet masterclass with move for ‘super’ teenage prospect

With Jeremy Jacquet already looking like a masterstroke of a signing, Liverpool could seek to replicate that coup with another transfer which’d bear strong echoes of the Frenchman’s arrival.

The right-back position at Anfield has been a volatile one since Trent Alexander-Arnold’s exit 18 months ago, with Conor Bradley sidelined by a serious knee injury and Jeremie Frimpong failing to truly convince since he joined in the summer of 2025 (whilst also suffering several injuries of his own).

It’s led to Andoni Iraola deploying the on-loan Ronald Araujo – conventionally a centre-back – on the right-hand side of defence, and thankfully the Uruguayan has been a sturdy presence in the Reds’ back four so far this season.

Nearly a year on from agreeing a deal to sign Jacquet, Liverpool could once more turn to Ligue 1 for a breakthrough defensive prospect.

According to Get French Football News, the Reds are currently monitoring Le Havre right-back Djibril Ouziad, who’s also being watched by Aston Villa.

The 17-year-old signed his first professional contract at the Stade Oceane in September, penning terms until 2030, but he’s deemed ‘likely to leave’ next summer even if his current club pull themselves out of the relegation zone in the French top flight.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Similar to how Jacquet properly established himself in Rennes’ first team last season, Ouziad is doing likewise with Le Havre this term, starting all but two of their league games so far in 2026/27 and making the right-back berth his own since being handed his senior debut in August.

A data analysis from Spencer Mossman highlighted the teenager as a ‘super creator’ who provides a serious threat from crosses and also marked him out as a ‘productive dribbler’ who’s likely to be ‘on a lot of radars very soon’.

The 17-year-old has been a rare plus point in a hithero miserable campaign for the Normandy outfit, and the creative influence that he provides from right-back seems reminiscent of Alexander-Arnold in his pomp at Liverpool.

What happens with Araujo’s future may well have a big bearing on whether or not the Reds go all-out to try and sign Ouziad. If the Uruguayan turns his loan move into a permanent transfer, there would be no great need for right-sided defensive reinforcements at Anfield.

However, if he goes back to Barcelona next summer and Frimpong were to depart amid rumours of Saudi Arabian interest, then Julian Ward might push hard in his attempts to snap up the Le Havre starlet.

#2014. Genoa 1-2 AC Milan: Five things we learned – battery life, the marksman and the core five

AC Milan managed to get the win that they needed going into the international break, but they certainly made hard work of it.

Things were going very well at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris against an in-form Genoa side, with Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic giving Milan a two-goal lead with less than 20 minutes on the clock. Both goals came from the high press, with Ruben Amorim’s side looking full of energy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, as has been the theme this year, the Rossoneri were unable to turn it into a complete performance. The second-half drop-off saw Genoa build more and more pressure, with Ellertsson’s strike from range making it a nervy finish.

Milan held on to secure a win that gets them back into the top four for now, and the search for consistency can resume after the two-week break. Oli Fisher has five things were learned from the game at the Marassi.

We are running out of words to describe this debut season for Alphadjo Cisse. If it wasn’t certain from the sample size we had already, then the Bologna games and this one today were proof that he is a right-place, right-time player.

The young Italian was perfectly positioned for Rabiot’s pull-back in the opening exchanges, as he so often is. He ghosts into scoring areas and provides the killer touch, with the goal this afternoon being perhaps his most impressive so far: a first-time finish across his body right into the corner.

The cynical side of us wants to say that Goncalo Ramos could learn a thing or two about what spots to be in inside the box, though the defence of the Portuguese is that his movement often creates these pockets of space to attack.

Cisse is one of only three players born in 2006 or later to have scored 8+ goals across all competitions in Europe’s top five leagues. The others are Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner (8). He also matched Andriy Shevchenko’s eight goals in his first 13 games for the Diavolo.

Another remarkable stat is that the 20-year-old has scored his eight goals across all competitions from just 20 shots. Some might argue that kind of hit rate is unsustainable, but it shows no signs of stopping for now.

As mentioned in the introduction, the first-half performance from Amorim’s side was something that fans can really get behind. It was intense, aggressive and front-footed. The quality wasn’t always there to turn everything into danger, but the intent was there.

In fact, it was this tenacity that yielded the two goals. The first one came after Pulisic pressed and won back possession, allowing Rabiot to square for Cisse. Then, the press again forced an error from Genoa with Ostigard’s stray pass seized by Ramos, who squared for Pulisic to net.

It serves as categorical proof that something energy levels alone can be enough to get Milan into very good positions in games. Yet, we also saw the other side of things too: when the battery runs flat, the Rossoneri can lose control of games very quickly.

As a result of this, where more polished teams might see things out comfortably or even score more goals, Milan seem to sink into a hole of self-doubt, inviting pressure through a quite obvious inability to cycle the ball and keep opponents at bay.

Injuries are partly to blame for this, because not having versatile options like Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Alexis Saelemaekers to bring on is hurting things. The bench on paper looked very weak, and those who did come in didn’t really help the chaos.

This is what Amorim refers to when he talks about the team not being ‘ready’. For various reasons – from the treatment room being full to the team not being fully cohesive – Milan’s level fluctuates wildly both within games and from match to match.

There was a report in La Gazzetta dello Sport this morning which highlighted a rather remarkable statistic. With Luka Modric, Mario Gila and Pulisic all not in the starting line-up, Milan are yet to pick up a single point.

This is arguably the crux of the rotation issue; the idea that managing the conditions of certain players is a necessity but upsetting the spine of the team is running a big risk. We’d like to add Rabiot and Diego Moreira into the mix too, as the five players Milan cannot do without.

The Spanish centre-back, the Croatian and French midfield duo, the Belgian wing-back and the American forward are simply too important. Their presence is vital not just because of their quality and propensity to provide decisive contributions, but because they are among the select group who can actually play Amorim’s way.

Each of them had a positive performance for various reasons. Gila’s fierce competitive nature facilitates the high line, Modric is the only one skilled in ball management, Rabiot is so wise when it comes to taking up the right positions, while Moreira and Pulisic are the technical sparks.

These are the players to build around from now until the end of season, while then waiting to see what the windows bring. When any combination of those five are playing, Milan’s limitations are often brutally exposed.

MilanNews described the performance from referee Davide Massa as a ‘disaster’, and we think that is being quite generous. The experienced official never once gave the impression of having control over a game where the pace and ferocity demanded it.

There is of course the one incident that everyone is talking about: the yellow card for Marcandalli after he brought Rabiot down. From our perspective, there are absolutely no doubts about it being a sending off.

The rules for DOGSO (Denial of a Goal Scoring Opportunity) take into account distance from goal, but the Frenchman and Cisse were about to have a two-on-zero attack with the entire half to run into. There is no way Ostigard was getting back to cover, and we question why VAR did not intervene.

To make matters worse, he then dished out a yellow card to Rabiot for rightfully protesting, and gave red cards to three of the Milan coaching staff too. In general Massa’s refereeing left a lot to be desired as there was no consistency in the fouls that he was whistling, and the five yellow cards the Rossoneri got felt disproportionate to Genoa’s two.

Thankfully the Diavolo were able to get over the line and bank the win, but if things had taken a more negative turn in the second half, we would be talking about that Marcandalli incident with a lot more venom.

Koni De Winter showed up in a big way against his old club, putting in another top performance in a week where he has been linked with a move to three big Premier League clubs.

Yet, we have to question the highs and lows. To best illustrate this, here are our ratings for the Belgian from each of the last four games.

vs. Bologna: Where to begin? I think he could have done better positioning-wise on Bologna’s first, with no one else to mark in the box, and then he completely gifted the free-kick that made it 2-1 for the guests. Some good moments too, but too many mistakes tonight. Maybe a 4.5?

vs. Inter (8): He absolutely won the battle against Thuram this game and it’s not like it was an easy one either. The two had several 50-50 duels and he always came out on top. Aside from his Thuram battle, he was very good overall and deserves a high rating here.

vs. Ferencvaros (5.5): That backpass for Torriani should never be played in that way, even if Maignan is between the sticks. He admittedly got a bit unlucky with his clearance in the second half, but even then perhaps he could have done better. Anyway, for me it’s the pass which brings his rating down.

vs. Genoa (7.5): The only poor moment came inside the first 60 seconds, when he was caught out a bit by a ball over the top, but he managed to track back and at least narrow the angle. After that, he was brilliant in his positioning, showing off with some great tackles and interceptions too. Really good.

Being the central centre-back is a position that carries a lot of weight and responsibility in Amorim’s system, and what is clear is that one game De Winter can look like the perfect man for the job, and in others he looks simply unplayable (and not in the good way).

One of the reasons for these wild fluctuations could also be because the former Juventus man simply hasn’t had a break. So, it is easy to see why the management are targeting a central defender ahead of January, someone who can give everyone a breather and help keep the levels high.

#2012. Manchester United sack Michael Carrick 10 days before Liverpool showdown

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick as head coach 10 days before their next fixture, which is against Liverpool at Anfield.

As was widely expected, the 45-year-old has paid the price for the Red Devils’ atrocious start to the season, with the Old Trafford outfit winning just one of their first 10 Premier League games and sitting in the relegation zone during the November international break.

Fabrizio Romano reported the news via X on Thursday morning, with other media outlets then confirming it before an official announcement from the club was communicated.

As per Sky Sports, Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be named as Carrick’s successor, with Man United having an agreement in place with the Argentine – currently in charge of the USA men’s national team – to take over after their CONCACAF Nations League in the coming week.

Should that impending appointment be completed in the anticipated timeframe, the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss would be in place in time for the Red Devils’ visit to Anfield on Sunday 22 November.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Although the practice of ‘new manager bounce’ isn’t exactly a scientific formula, a myriad of case studies – a few of which involve Man United – may have injected trepidation into Liverpool fans ahead of the grudge match in L4 on Sunday week.

Carrick himself took over a Red Devils team in turmoil last January and, in his first two games, oversaw wins over Manchester City and Arsenal, who ultimately finished second and first in the Premier League.

Eight years ago, after Jose Mourinho got the sack at Old Trafford following a comprehensive defeat at Anfield, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer triggered an immediate upturn in form which saw them pick up 25 points from a possible 27 in the top flight.

Managerial changes aside, Man United have an annoying habit of pulling out a result against Liverpool when it’s least expected. In January 2025, they were 14th in the table when they faced the table-topping Reds on Merseyside and came away with a 2-2 draw.

Iraola has already tasted defeat twice at Anfield this season (against Man City and Arsenal). Another on Sunday week would rankle the most of all, especially when our arch-rivals have been so abysmal over the past three months but conveniently trigger a change just in time for their visit to L4.

#2011. Ex-CEO updates on Leicester City 'terminating' agreement

Leicester City cannot afford to terminate their deal with their front-of-shirt sponsor BC Game any time soon.

That is according to former Aston Villa chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that it will be "very hard" for the Foxes to enforce a "morality clause" in the agreement.

This comes after the gambling company BC Game recently named a porn actress as one of their new ambassadors, a move which has quickly been condemned by fan group The Foxes Trust.

However, Wyness believes that it will be "very difficult" in a legal sense for Leicester to terminate the deal, and also pointed out that they need the money it is providing right now.

The League One outfit are struggling on the pitch and remain in turmoil at board level behind the scenes.

Long-time owners King Power are working to sell the club, but are making slow progress with their move to cash in on the East Midlands outfit.

Villa's former chief Wyness - who served as CEO at Villa Park between 2016 and 2018 and now runs a consultancy business advising elite clubs - believes that Leicester may be forced to just accept the "publicity" that has come with BC Game's move.

The Foxes' fans have raised questions regarding the morality of the deal and the image it presents, but Wyness is adamant that the club are not in a position to be axing partners.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, he believes that the club must simply sweep the story under the carpet before it becomes a "distraction."

"No, I think they have to stay with it. I think they need the money. And I think that it will be very difficult legally to terminate the deal as well," he said.

"Normally, if there is a morality clause, which often is in there, it would be about the behaviour of the company itself. And if she is legally hired as an ambassador by the company and she's not done anything wrong in her past, it would be very hard to enforce a morality clause, in my opinion.

"So I don't think they'd have great grounds to terminate. Look, if I were them, I'd take the publicity. I'd move on. Leicester need the money. It's a distraction.

"But look, I'm afraid, as I said, we've seen stories of clubs who are desperate for sponsors and revenue. And it's not always easy to dictate the behaviour of your sponsors."

Football Insider revealed back in October that Leicester had held internal talks about potentially replacing Russell Martin as manager.

The Foxes had their eyes set on former Wolves boss Rob Edwards, who recently turned down an approach from Championship strugglers Burnley.

However, Leicester have since embarked on a four-match unbeaten run, which has lifted them up to tenth in League One amid the latest international break.

Things are beginning to look brighter for Martin and his group, but they still have huge expectations to fulfill this season.

#2008. GdS: Fluidity, gifts and a tense finale – how Milan overcame Genoa to reclaim top four spot

AC Milan won away from home against an in-form Genoa side to ensure they will go into the international break inside the top four.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) have analysed a second consecutive Serie A victory for Milan, remarking that if it were it not for the nuisance of the Europa League – specifically that ugly defeat to Ferencváros – they would be heading into the break in perfect spirits.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Still, things have worked out well enough: the win at Marassi, combined with Como’s loss against Inter, has allowed Rúben Amorim’s side to leapfrog Cesc Fàbregas’s team and move into fourth place. It is of course the final spot for Champions League qualification, the minimum objective.

The question remains the same: which is the ‘real’ Milan? The one that put two goals past Genoa in the opening 20 minutes, or the one that nearly threw it all away with a passive final 20 minutes of the game?

Daniele De Rossi almost snatched a point thanks to his substitutions, while Amorim nearly dropped two points due to his own, less-than-effective changes. It seems clear that there is an issue with the squad’s overall competitiveness, with help needed in January.

In Genoa, Amorim opted for a 4-4-2 formation to start, with Yunus Musah deployed as a surprise left-back and a central midfield pairing of Luka Modrić and Adrien Rabiot.

Just seconds after kick-off, Genoa nearly took a 1-0 lead through Osmajic, who surged deep into the final third. Shaken into life by this, Milan took control and built a 2-0 lead.

In the second half, the team gradually shifted into a classic 3-5-2, eventually dropping into a five-man defensive line to hold firm after Ellertsson’s goal. In modern football, fluidity is an asset though it carries the risk of lacking a clear, defined identity.

Milan dominated for long stretches of the first half, particularly on the flanks, but found themselves under significant duress toward the end of the match. The data on the average position of the team is telling: Genoa finished at 55.6 metres, while Milan sat at 44.3.

Anyone unaware of the final score when looking at the stats might well imagine a different outcome, while it remains unclear if the team dropping so deep was instruction or protective instinct. However, the Diavolo survived.

The reality is that sometimes errors – individual or otherwise – have a greater impact on results than good intentions or tactical formations. Genoa arrived at this match on the back of three consecutive victories, though they were missing Frendrup, the Dane who acts as the team’s stabiliser.

Having already enjoyed a string of successes, the team grew complacent. It was a feeling only intensified by the golden opportunity that fell to Osmajic in the opening minutes. Genoa lulled themselves into a false sense of security, and some players began to switch off.

There was an early warning sign when Vasquez gifted the ball to Gonçalo Ramos, though the Portuguese forward’s shot went wide. Later, Vasquez was dispossessed again – this time by Pulisic – sparking the sequence that led to the 0-1 goal: a touch to Rabiot, a cross for Cissé and a finish.

Milan then shifted their focus to the left flank. Under pressure from Cissé, Traoré played a disastrous pass toward Østigård inside the box. The Norwegian failed to clear it, and Ramos set up Pulisic just inside the area for the goal that made it 0-2.

At 2-0, the game opened up for Milan, who favoured direct, vertical play over patient possession. The attacking combinations on the flanks proved decisive: Moreira operated on one side, working alongside Pulisic, who was given the freedom to roam between the penalty area, the final third, and the wing.

The duo of Musah and Cissé dominated their flank against Marcandalli and Ehizibue. Deploying Musah as a left-back was a tactical move De Rossi likely hadn’t anticipated. Was it all over? Had the match been decided? Not quite. Before the half-time whistle, Genoa showed signs of a resurgence.

In the second half, the atmosphere turned hostile, and referee Massa had to send four people off from the benches to restore some semblance of order. Then, a flurry of substitutions narrowed the gap between Genoa and Milan.

When El Shaarawy came on, De Rossi found more space to push forward. When Pulisic was taken off, Amorim’s side lost ground. Ellertsson’s goal – a beautiful strike, aided by a lack of marking from Jashari – set the stall out for a frantic final stretch, during which Milan risked conceding an equaliser.

if you tally up the chances and shots on target, the scales actually tip in favor of the Grifone. So, what does this mean? Is all well that ends well? Is a Champions League spot guaranteed? Certainly not. The impression is that this Milan is still in a phase where anything is possible, in either direction.

A return to the Champions League is far from certain, but the table is tight. League-leaders Lazio are only five points ahead, less than two wins away, so who’s to say Milan can’t aim higher?

Much will depend on January. The winter window shouldn’t be about patching things up, as quick fixes often end up being worse than the original problems. Rather, Gerry Cardinale (plus potentially Markus Krösche) should think about genuine improvement.

It will also depend on Amorim and his ability to shape the squad, ironing out the deficiencies. In the background, the question of Gonçalo Ramos remains. He showed commendable selflessness at Marassi, but he needs to start scoring himself soon.

For now, Cissé is stepping up, having netted his eighth goal of the season and his fifth in Serie A. Roberto Mancini is now waiting for him with the senior national team, which is just the latest step in a fairytale start to 2026-27.

#2006. AFC Wimbledon vs Blackpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 11 Nov 2026 14:40, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 14:46

Returning to League One action after competing in the opening round of the FA Cup, AFC Wimbledon welcome Blackpool to Plough Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Dons suffered a 2-1 defeat to League Two outfit Crewe Alexandra last weekend, while the Seasiders survived a scare against Hornchurch, needing a 118th-minute winner to book their place in the second round, where they will face Salisbury.

Playing their first league match since Halloween, Johnnie Jackson and his Wimbledon side will be desperate to end a run of six league games without a victory, and 10 matches without a win across all competitions, when they take on a Blackpool side they have avoided defeat against in each of their previous five meetings.

With that said, the Dons are unlikely to have entered any previous meeting with the Seasiders in worse form than they find themselves in currently, having followed a 1-0 victory over Doncaster Rovers on September 12 with three league draws and six defeats, while also suffering early exits from the EFL Trophy and FA Cup during their difficult spell.

Taking on high-flying Stockport County at the end of October, Wimbledon entered the final stages with a one-goal advantage but conceded late strikes from Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis to suffer another damaging defeat, before facing Crewe last weekend as favourites to progress in the FA Cup.

However, their journey in football's oldest competition came to a premature end as they suffered a 2-1 defeat against fourth-tier Crewe, with Charlie McNeill producing a memorable moment by scoring from the halfway line inside the opening 12 minutes.

With no further cup commitments until next season, Jackson and his side can now focus entirely on their League One campaign as they look to rediscover some much-needed form and move further away from the relegation zone.

As for Blackpool, they avoided an FA Cup upset at the weekend when they faced National League outfit Hornchurch, although Ian Evatt's side were forced to take the scenic route before eventually booking their place in the second round after extra time.

The Seasiders went into the break a goal behind but emerged with renewed purpose and soon drew level through a sweetly struck Jordan Brown volley, before Josh Bowler struck deep into extra time to spare their blushes and prevent what would have been a significant cup upset.

That victory means Evatt's side are now unbeaten in three matches, following an EFL Trophy win over Aston Villa Under-21s and a 1-1 draw away to Sheffield Wednesday, who spent the majority of that league encounter with 10 men.

While just one defeat in their last five matches across all competitions represents a notable improvement for the Seasiders, they still head into their 13th League One fixture of the campaign dangerously close to the relegation zone.

Three wins, three draws and six defeats have given Blackpool a slender one-point cushion over 21st-placed Wigan Athletic, although they do have games in hand on several of the sides immediately above them, while a victory this weekend would see them leapfrog Wimbledon, who currently sit 18th on 13 points.

Following the disappointing defeat to Crewe, Jackson could make a number of changes to his starting XI, although Wimbledon emerged from the cup tie without any fresh injury concerns.

Andy Yiadom came off the bench on Saturday and marked his appearance with a goal, potentially earning himself a starting opportunity for this fixture, with Isaac Ogundere among those most at risk of dropping out.

The Dons remain without forward Mathew Stevens, who continues to recover from a hamstring injury that has kept him sidelined since March.

Stevens scored 26 league goals for Wimbledon across the previous two seasons and has since been replaced by Jayden Stockley, who has impressed during his maiden campaign at the club and is expected to lead the line again as he looks to add to the six League One goals he has scored in 13 appearances.

Blackpool also had a substitute make an immediate impact last time out, with Bowler finding the net from the bench to strengthen his case for a return to the starting XI in London.

Fraser Horsfall made his long-awaited return to action at the end of October in the EFL Trophy but suffered another setback and is set to miss a third consecutive match, having last started a game in April.

The Tangerines are also without Irish midfielder CJ Hamilton and 33-year-old defender Michael Ihiekwe, who are recovering from knee ligament and muscle injuries respectively, while George Honeyman and Niall Ennis are also expected to remain in the treatment room, adding to Evatt's growing list of absentees.

In the absence of captain Honeyman, Karoy Anderson is expected to wear the armband in the centre of midfield.

#2003. Prickly Unai Emery fires back at 'more questions' from Sky Sports reporter in awkward interview after storming down Old Trafford tunnel before full time

By JAMES DUTTON, DEPUTY SPORTS NEWS EDITOR

Published: 16:35 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 17:09 EST, 8 November 2026

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery was in a prickly mood as he bit back at Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davison in a fiery end to his post-match interview at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Emery had just seen his Villa side twice throw away a two-goal lead against Manchester United – with Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scoring in stoppage time to secure a remarkable 4-4 draw.

The Villa boss was spotted storming down the touchline before the full-time whistle and after Dorgu's dramatic 97th-minute equaliser – with play continuing for another two minutes.

And the Villa boss, already exasperated at being asked 'more questions,' did not take kindly to being asked if he was emotional about the late equaliser or if he felt it was unfair.

When asked if his walking off was an emotional reaction, he responded: 'No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I [thought] the match was finishing.'

And then when asked whether the award of the goal was unfair, he replied: 'No, no. Not unfair. Please.

Unai Emery was in a prickly mood towards the end of his post match interview with Sky Sports

Emery had just stormed down the tunnel at Old Trafford after Aston Villa threw away a 4-2 lead in stoppage time

Emery took exception to being asked 'more questions' by Sky reporter Patrick Davison

'They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off.'

Emery ended the interview making light of his 'poor' English, and then sarcastically asking if there were 'more questions' before an ironic 'Have a good Sunday' as he walked out of the interview.

Villa's director of football operations Damian Vidagany complained on social media about the legitimacy of United's last-gasp equaliser.

He accused United goalkeeper Senne Lammens – who went up for the corner – of impeding his Villa counterpart Zion Suzuki as he looked to punch the ball clear.

After Roy Keane said 'football is a contact sport,' he posted on X: 'To put in context this convenient narrative of "contact sport" we've been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six-yard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

'Lammens did not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

'Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last six minutes. We will do and we will improve.

'But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact.'

Michael Carrick was involved in a spiky interview with Sky Sports about his Man United future

Sky Sports' Davison's brush with Emery came just minutes after a spiky interview with beleaguered United boss Michael Carrick.

When the future of his own position was put to him by Davison, Carrick took exception to the question.

'What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? You've been asked time and again about your future? I know you have said that you walking away was the best for the club, you'd probably do it,' Davison asked Carrick.

'It's not going to happen, no,' Carrick replied.

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week. They conceded twice at the start of each half against Villa, and have now let in 30 goals in all competitions – the joint highest in Europe's top five leagues.

#2001. Nottingham Forest could make Zach Abbott U-turn after Southampton development - verdict

Correspondent AUTHORITY Football journalist with experience at Reach PLC and PA Media; University of Central Lancashire graduate. FOCUS Fan-engagement content and match analysis across the Premier League and Championship. THE INSIGHT Oliver utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified reporting and fan-first content. He provides the human stories behind the results to ensure fans get the full picture as it happens.

Nottingham Forest may decide to keep Zach Abbott on loan at Southampton as more minutes beckon for him in a promotion-chasing side.

Oliver Glasner saw fit to allow Abbott out on loan in the summer, as he joined Southampton for the rest of the campaign on Deadline Day.

The 20-year-old defender signed a new long-term contract extension with his boyhood club upon agreeing to the loan move, proving just how highly rated he is at the City Ground.

His time at St Mary's has certainly not gone to plan so far, with just two appearances in their bid to win promotion back to the Premier League.

Recent reports have claimed that Forest are ready to recall him in January, but they may now be handed an incentive not to as Abbott pushes to start regularly under Tonda Eckert.

Keven Schlotterbeck's long-term injury is set to open the door for Abbott to receive more game time, as he looks to nail down a spot in their main eleven in the absence of the German.

Abbott's short Forest career has shown promise, with several decent performances in their run to the Europa League semi-finals last season.

He played regularly under Glasner in pre-season, and so it has likely come as a surprise to the 20-year-old and those at Forest to see him utilised so sparingly at Southampton this season.

Abbott was forced to wait over a month for his Saints debut, then was hooked off at half-time against Norwich on 14 October and failed to appear in any of their next four games.

Schlotterbeck's early injury last time out against Preston saw Abbott introduced from the bench, and he impressed despite a shock 1-0 defeat.

New reports have since claimed that the commanding German centre-back faces around six weeks on the sidelines.

Abbott looks to be in pole position to take his place in the starting eleven, meaning Forest may not be forced to recall him after all, especially if he does well and nails down a spot in the side.

Abbott won all three of his attempted duels against Preston, completed 90 per cent of his passes and made four clearances in a stellar showing from the cold.

Eckert praised his young loanee after the clash, saying: "He was very positive. I think he's done very well. It was not an easy game to come into, especially with the amount of long balls he had to deal with, and I think he's done that well."

Abbott will surely be the man to take Schlotterbeck's place in the team after the international break, and that will be music to the ears of Forest coaches and chiefs who want him to progress and return a better player next summer.

#2000. Next Man United manager: Why Darren Fletcher could be set for interim head coach role while Red Devils wait for Mauricio Pochettino

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 15:56, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 16:04

USA are reportedly still expecting head coach Mauricio Pochettino to lead them into their two November internationals against Haiti.

Pochettino has allegedly come to an agreement with Manchester United over personal terms and is set to become their new head coach, should Michael Carrick, as expected, be sacked.

As of Wednesday afternoon, there is still no communication from Man United over a departure for Carrick, but the Englishman is set to lose his job over the next 24 hours.

Pochettino is the red-hot favourite for the role at Old Trafford, and it is understood that an agreement in principle with the Argentine's representatives has been reached.

However, according to The Independent's Miguel Delaney, there is "still some way to go".

The publication claims that the United States are expecting Pochettino to lead them into their two matches against Haiti on November 14 and November 18 respectively.

Man United, though, are pushing to have Pochettino available sooner, given that the team will be back in Premier League action against Liverpool on November 22.

There is allegedly an option to appoint Darren Fletcher as an interim head coach once again, should Man United be unable to conclude a deal quickly.

Fletcher, who is the head coach of Man United Under-18s, was the club's caretaker head coach in January following the sacking of Ruben Amorim.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada met with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's future.

An announcement regarding Carrick's removal as head coach could come on Thursday.

Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann are all available for an immediate start and have been linked with the position at Old Trafford.

However, Pochettino has emerged as the club's number one choice.

Pochettino has a contract with the United States until the end of the 2030 World Cup, and Man United need to pay a £7.4m compensation fee to bring him to Old Trafford, with further fees required to appoint his trusted coaching staff, including assistant Jesus Perez.

A difficult start to the 2026-27 campaign has left Man United down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, winning just once in England's top flight this term.

#1999. “It’s a special place” – Liverpool confirm Anfield return for James Milner

Liverpool FC have confirmed on Thursday that James Milner will return to Anfield in 2027.

Signed on a free transfer from Manchester City in 2015, the former Reds midfielder spent eight years on Merseyside and became vice-captain under Jurgen Klopp, winning the Premier League and Champions League among other trophies in his time with the club.

The 40-year-old closed out his playing career at Brighton, announcing his retirement this summer after setting the record for the most Premier League seasons appeared in (24 consecutively from 2002/03 to 2025/26).

As announced via liverpoolfc.com on Thursday lunchtime, Milner is the first player to be confirmed for the next Liverpool Legends match, which takes place against Inter Milan at Anfield on Saturday 27 March 2027, with proceeds going towards the LFC Foundation.

The Reds’ former vice-captain said of his participation in the fixture: “I’m thrilled to have the chance to pull on the red shirt again and step back out at Anfield. It’s a special place, and playing there in front of the supporters is a feeling like no other.

“What makes the legends match so special is that it’s about more than football. It’s a chance to give something back to the fans while supporting the work of the LFC Foundation. I’m delighted to be the first to sign up and can’t wait to be part of it.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The news of Milner’s participation in the 2027 Legends match is sure to go down a treat with Liverpool fans who adored him for his humility and commitment to the cause in his eight years as a Red, along with his excellence as a player.

The Yorkshire native was renowned for setting exceptionally high standards within the playing group and enjoyed near-annual domination of the infamous pre-season lactate test, and he commands universal respect among his peers and the wider football community.

The Reds were lucky enough to be the club that he represented more times than any other, with 322 of his 903 senior appearances coming for the Merseysiders (Transfermarkt).

He’ll now get to line out in a Liverpool shirt at Anfield once more, and while it mightn’t be in a competitive fixture, the reception won’t be any less rapturous for a player whose supreme attitude characterised a glorious era for LFC.

As ever, it promises to be a wonderful occasion in which thousands of pounds will be raised for a most worthy cause, and Kopites will get to enjoy seeing many former greats of the club return for one afternoon.

#1998. Aston Villa 'will not entertain' Boubacar Camara offers amid 'serious' injury worries - expert

Aston Villa are not prepared to entertain any offers for Boubacar Kamara in the January transfer window or beyond.

The 26-year-old remains a crucial part of Unai Emery's plans, having started 14 games across all competitions this season, including all ten in the Premier League.

Meanwhile, there are concerns about a lack of strength in depth in central midfield areas, where Amadou Onana's long-term injury has caused further complications.

Former Aston Villa scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Emery has no plans to weaken his squad, and Onana's injury means no midfielders will be sold in January.

Kamara has attracted high-profile interest from a number of European clubs, most recently including Chelsea and Inter Milan, as well as some in the Saudi Pro League.

However, he is regarded as a key part of this Aston Villa squad, and the club will not entertain offers for the France international ahead of the January transfer window.

Former Aston Villa scout Bryan King told Football Insider on 12 November that Kamara is one of just three players in Emery's starting XI whose position is currently guaranteed.

The midfielder continues to play a crucial role in the midfield, as he has done as long as he has been fit since his arrival at the club in 2022.

As a result, there are not plans to let Kamara leave the club any time soon, and concerns about a lack of midfield depth and Onana's long-term injury will not support an exit.

"Kamara is still a very important player for Aston Villa, he's playing every week at the moment," Brown told Football Insider.

"Unai Emery likes him, he sees him as an important part of their plans, so I expect Villa will not be entertaining any offers for him, regardless of who might be interested.

"They're not exactly blessed with an abundance of midfield talent, it's an area where they will probably have to improve, so they're not going to be prepared to weaken there.

"Plus, you've got Onana there who has been ruled out for a long time with a serious injury, so that makes any decision to sell midfielders complicated.

"They're already lacking depth, and with Onana out, that's a big asset and a big influence who is missing, so they certainly won't want to lose Kamara as well."

Kamara is not the only midfielder whose future at Aston Villa has been up for discussion in recent weeks, with speculation starting to circle ahead of the January transfer window.

Ross Barkley has recently faced questions about his long-term future at Villa Park, with his increased role in the first-team squad meaning Villa could be forced into a decision.

Brown told Football Insider on 29 October that Aston Villa are planning to offer Barkley a contract extension to ensure he remains at the club beyond next summer.

Doubts had crept in surrounding the midfielder's future in the summer, when he was linked with a move away, and could grow again if he does not extend his deal.

However, after Emery branded Barkley "a very good player" and praised his experience and recent performances, work is now ongoing to ensure he remains part of his plans.

#1997. Steven Gerrard identifies Lamine Yamal challenge after Messi and Ronaldo comparison

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 15:56

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard believes Lamine Yamal is already more advanced than Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo were at 19, but has identified the major challenge that could determine whether the Barcelona youngster eventually matches their extraordinary achievements.

The former England captain has been hugely impressed by Yamal's development, describing the Spanish international as a player capable of reaching the level established by two of football's greatest names.

However, Gerrard believes maintaining the hunger to win throughout a long career will be just as important as the teenager's natural ability.

He has also questioned whether Yamal may eventually need to move into a central attacking role to approach the remarkable goalscoring records accumulated by Messi and Ronaldo.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Gerrard drew on his own experience of facing both players during their early years to explain why he considers Barcelona's latest academy graduate such an exceptional prospect.

Gerrard, who faced Ronaldo during the Portuguese forward's Manchester United career and encountered Messi in European competition, believes Yamal has reached an unusually advanced stage of development for his age.

"He's more advanced than Ronaldo was at 19," Gerrard said.

The former Liverpool midfielder also suggested that Yamal was further along in his development than Messi had been at the same stage, while acknowledging the challenge of sustaining that progress.

His assessment reflects the enormous impact Yamal has already made since breaking into Barcelona's first team in April 2023.

The Spain international, who celebrated his 19th birthday in July, has established himself as a central figure in Hansi Flick's attack despite continuing to operate predominantly from the right wing.

Yamal has registered 13 goals and 12 assists in 16 appearances across all competitions during the 2026-27 campaign, maintaining an extraordinary level of productivity for a player still in his teenage years.

His development has been accompanied by major international success, having helped Spain win Euro 2024 before adding the 2026 World Cup to his honours.

The winger has also finished second and third in the last two Ballon d'Or rankings, recognition of the influence he has already established at the highest level.

By comparison, Messi was still developing into a regular goalscorer during his teenage years at Barcelona, while Ronaldo's early seasons at Manchester United were defined more by his dribbling and individual creativity than the prolific finishing that would later characterise his career.

Ronaldo scored nine goals in 50 appearances during the 2004-05 campaign, a season in which he turned 20.

Yamal had already surpassed that figure at 17, scoring 18 times for Barcelona in 2024-25.

Yet Gerrard is reluctant to conclude that the Spaniard's remarkable start guarantees a career comparable to either of those legends.

For Gerrard, the central question concerns whether Yamal can retain the same ambition and consistency over the next decade.

The former Liverpool captain believes Barcelona's coaching staff and the people closest to the youngster will have a crucial role in keeping him motivated after such an extraordinary start to his career.

"The biggest challenge for him - and those around him at Barcelona - is how they keep him hungry?" Gerrard asked.

He believes Yamal must continue pursuing collective trophies and individual recognition even as success becomes a familiar part of his career.

The difficulty is particularly significant given the standards established by Messi and Ronaldo, whose greatest achievements were built upon sustained performances over many seasons.

Both players also developed into exceptional goalscorers after initially establishing themselves in wider attacking positions.

Gerrard therefore raised the possibility that Yamal's long-term evolution could involve a similar positional adjustment.

The 19-year-old is currently most influential when starting from the right, where his close control, ability to eliminate defenders and vision allow him to create opportunities for teammates.

Moving into a central position could theoretically increase his goalscoring opportunities, although Gerrard presented the idea as a possibility for later in his career rather than an immediate recommendation to Flick.

Yamal's existing production suggests that he does not need such a change to contribute heavily in front of goal.

His 25 direct goal involvements this season also underline why he continues to attract comparisons with Messi, whose development at Barcelona remains an obvious reference point.

Gerrard's comments follow those of former Barcelona loanee Marcus Rashford, who recently identified Yamal as the closest player he had encountered to Messi's level.

The Manchester United forward, who spent the 2025-26 season alongside Yamal, also expressed his belief in the youngster's potential to compete for multiple Ballon d'Or awards.

Gerrard shares that admiration, but his comparison carries an important qualification: Yamal may be ahead of Messi and Ronaldo at 19, yet matching what they achieved over the course of their careers will demand a level of consistency that remains impossible to judge at such an early stage.
