#1952. Sky: Ramos involved but has minimal support – the numbers that illustrate Amorim’s point

Some interesting analysis on AC Milan and Goncalo Ramos’ attacking struggles has been provided by the Sky studios.

It was a familiar tale for Ramos during Milan’s 2-1 win over Genoa on Sunday. He was involved but rarely inside the box, then he was selfless instead of ruthless in front of goal when he chose to square for Christian Pulisic to make it 2-0.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The worries are starting to grow regarding whether the Portuguese can provide the output required of a number nine that cost €70m. Yet, the Rossoneri have scored 23 goals in 11 league games which suggests goals are coming from elsewhere, sometimes with Ramos’ help.

Sky offered some interesting insight after Sunday’s game. Firstly, they picked out just how involved Ramos actually is with various aspects of Milan’s overall play.

For example, he is first among Serie A strikers for interceptions and recoveries, while he is second for receptions, touches and duels. He is third for passes.

He is first among centre-forwards in the league for touches in the middle third of the field and touches in the opposition half. He is second for fouls committed plus fouls suffered among forwards, with 41.

Sky then shift the focus to the team’s overall play to try and explain why Ramos perhaps isn’t getting the quality service and is having to drop deeper as a result.

They look at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. With numbers like these, there isn’t much for Ramos to get on the end of.

What does this tell us? Well, Amorim’s post match assessment about struggling to get the ball from the defensive third into the final third are true. Milan have a lot of the ball but still struggle to progress it, as the coach told Sky.

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals,” he said.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

Man United overhauled their midfield during the summer transfer window, bringing in Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, but it would be fair to say that the balance in the middle of the park is still not quite right at this moment in time.

As a result, there is expected to be space in the squad for another midfield arrival, and bringing in Scott from Bournemouth would be a huge statement of intent.

The 23-year-old - valued in the region of £80m by Bournemouth - is also wanted by Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool.

The loss came after an encouraging weekend when the Rooks secured a 3-2 win at Dulwich Hamlet.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The pair of fixtures began with a trip to Champion Hill, where the Rooks enjoyed their best away day of the 2025-26 season with a 4-1 win in mid-December.

They repeated that feat with another thoroughly impressive performance, responding to a 43rd-minute opener from the hosts with a standout second half.

Goals from Kurtis Cumberbatch, Josh Spinks and Bobby Unwin saw the Rooks roar into control in the gathering South London fog, with an added-time Dulwich response proving to be a consolation.

Lewes shared their celebrations with a large set of supporters at full-time.

Nelson said of the Rooks fans: “They're unreal. We always try to repay them regardless of what the score is, but here feels a little bit special.

“Even at the beginning of the season, they all talked about Dulwich away and making sure we can come here and put out a performance they can go home and be proud of, and they were noisy.

“[Tyler] Cox came over to me and said, ‘They've been unbelievable. I can't wait to get back on the pitch just to clap for them,’ and that's what it means. They were our 12th man, and it's a pleasure to be able to stand in front of them with three points.”

With their trip to Enfield having been rescheduled to a Tuesday night, Lewes had an uphill task against a side in title contention.

The Rooks began their season with a 4-0 loss to the North London side, and while they started much better on the road, reaching half-time at a stalemate, the hosts’ quality eventually won out.

“I think we're looking at the champions of the league,” said Nelson.

“I felt we had to ride a lot of waves in the first half, but we dug in to keep it nil-nil, and then ran out of luck.

“It's probably the first time I've stood in front of you guys and said that we were totally outplayed, outclassed, outmatched, outrun, and outduelled. So I think you can't ever stand on the other side of that and expect to get anything from the game.”

Another busy week awaits the Rooks, with a home meeting with Isthmian Premier Division basement club Stanway Rovers this Saturday (3pm kick-off) before a Sussex Senior Cup trip to Eastbourne Town on Tuesday night (7.45pm).

#1949. Andy Robertson: My 102 caps is a chance to recognise what Sir Kenny Dalglish did - not me

Scotland captain Andy Robertson claims his 102nd cap should be a reason to celebrate Sir Kenny Dalglish and not himself as he prepares to join his fellow former Liverpool player as record appearance holder.

The 32-year-old will draw level with Dalglish when he leads Scotland out at Hampden on Friday against North Macedonia in the Nations League.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“Tomorrow’s not really about me,” the Tottenham left-back said. “It’s about him in my opinion. For how long the record stood, for what he achieved in his career, for the person he is.

“It’s another reason for our country to tip our hat to one of the greatest players that have played the game, never mind in Scotland, he’s definitely the greatest in Scotland.”

Robertson was speaking on the 40th anniversary of Dalglish’s final international, a 3-0 win over Luxembourg when he was in his second season as Liverpool player/manager.

“That tells you everything that you need to know, the fact that he’s juggling all that and still showing up for his country,” Robertson said. “He reminds me all the time that 102 caps back then was a lot harder than 102 caps now, and he’s right because there were less games.

“In terms of numbers, I’ll stand side by side with him, but I don’t want people to forget how important this man has been for our country. He was arguably the best player in the world at his time and he’ll always be the greatest in this country.”

Dalglish recently joked that he hoped Robertson would retire before he sets a new record. “We’ve had a lot of jokes, but I also know deep down how proud he is of me and how happy he is for me as well,” the former Dundee United player said. “I always remember when I got the captaincy, he was one of the first people to text me and say, ‘I know I’ve been out of the game maybe a little bit, but if you need help, if you need somebody to bounce anything off, then I can be that person’.

“To have somebody like that, that you can bounce anything off and rely on, him and his family have been such a massive help to my family, especially in my time at Liverpool.

“I’ve got no doubt there’ll be a couple of texts that will get exchanged. I know we laugh and we joke, publicly and privately, but I know he’s proud of me and he’s happy for what I’ve achieved as well.”

Robertson is set to surpass Dalglish in Switzerland on Monday and he is no mood to slow down. “I’m still hungry to achieve more for the country,” he said. “I want to get Scotland back to another major tournament, I want to try and get out the group stages.

“Secondly, I want to try and leave the squad in the best possible place in terms of the quality coming through, the characters they’ve got, the mentality they’ve got.

“If I can leave that behind, then I can maybe enjoy Scotland games a bit more and I can join the fans and party with them.”

By Lewis Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 18:15

Andorra will conclude their Nations League D campaign on Friday, when they welcome Gibraltar to Estadi de la FAF d'Encamp.

The hosts are last in their three-team group with one point from their three matches so far, whereas the visitors are second with two points from two games.

Andorra were beaten 1-0 by Malta on October 4 in their latest outing in the competition, with their only point coming in a 0-0 stalemate with Gibraltar on September 27.

All three teams in their group will be competing in Nations League C in 2028-29, but while there is no jeopardy for either team on Friday, their placement in group will determine their rankings for the next campaign.

The hosts have only scored one goal in the group so far, though they have conceded just three times in the group stage.

Boss Koldo Alvarez has been in charge of the national team for 16 years, but he has only overseen 13 wins from his 146 games in the dugout, and he has lost 15, drawn five and won just one of his last 21 matches as head coach.

Andorra's performances at home have been poor considering they have been beaten in six of their past seven fixtures when playing as hosts.

Gibraltar are in arguably their best ever period of form given they are undefeated in their last six fixtures in all competitions, winning on three occasions.

The visitors managed to score 11 goals and concede just twice, and they kept four clean sheets in that time.

It should be noted that Los Llanis did play Liechtenstein, Cayman Islands, British Virgin Islands and Sao Tome and Principe in those six clashes, with the latter the highest-ranked nation by FIFA at 194th.

Head coach Scott Wiseman will hope to avoid becoming the first manager in his country's history to lose against Andorra, with his side having won two times and settled for two stalemates in four meetings with their hosts.

Gibraltar have been defeated in five of their seven most recent contests on the road, with their only victory in that period a 2-0 success against Liechtenstein on October 5.

Andorra could use a four-man defence featuring central defenders Max Llovera and Ian Bryan Olivera ahead of goalkeeper Iker Alvarez.

Midfielders Ot Remolins Planes and Eric Vales could be rewarded with their 11th and 25th caps for the national team.

In the frontline, it would not be surprising to see forward Albert Rosas partnered by Guillaume Lopez, with the duo having scored five and two goals respectively for the hosts.

As for Gibraltar, it would not be surprising to see Dan Bent, Bernardo Lopes and Julian Valarino form a back three, especially after the trio started in the reverse fixture against their hosts.

Leon Mason and Nicholas Pozo may be used as two third of a midfield three, while Tjay De Barr and Dylan Borge are set to start up front.

Alvarez; Font, Llovera, Olivera, Nicolas; Alaez, Planes, Vales, Rodrigo; Rosas, Lopez

Banda; Bent, Lopes, Valarino; Ronan, Mason, Torrilla, Pozo, Scanlon; De Barr, Borge

Neither side are likely to be at their best considering there is little to play for given all teams will be in Nations League C.

However, with Andorra backed by a home crowd, perhaps the hosts will be able take at least a point against Gibraltar, who have often travelled poorly.

#1944. Cape Verde vs Liberia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 11 Nov 2026 18:45

Cape Verde will be looking to get their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign off the mark when they welcome Liberia to the Estadio Nacional de Cabo Verde in Praia on Friday evening.

The Blue Sharks sit third in Group K after back-to-back defeats to Mali and Rwanda, while the visitors are bottom of the table and also without a point.

Cape Verde have made a disappointing start to the post-World Cup era, losing both of their opening Group K matches under new head coach Humberto Bettencourt.

They were beaten 3-1 by Mali before suffering a 2-1 home defeat to Rwanda, in which Gilson Benchimol's 40th-minute strike was cancelled out before half-time and the visitors scored again seven minutes into the second half.

Bettencourt, who spent six years as Bubista's assistant, has overseen two defeats in his first two competitive matches, leaving the Blue Sharks winless in their last six games (D3, L3), a run that includes goalless World Cup draws with Spain and Saudi Arabia, a 2-2 draw with Uruguay and a 3-2 round-of-32 defeat to Argentina.

However, their previous meetings with Liberia offer some encouragement, as Cape Verde have won three of the four encounters between the sides, including a 4-1 home victory in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in March 2011.

Liberia, meanwhile, began their qualifying campaign with a 3-1 defeat in Kigali, where Sylvanus Nimely scored their only goal before Rwanda restored their two-goal advantage from the penalty spot in the 44th minute.

The Lone Star then suffered a 1-0 home defeat to Mali, with Martial Tia's 79th-minute strike settling the contest.

Moroccan coach Mohammed Adil Erradi, who took charge of his first competitive match in Kigali, is still waiting for his first victory.

Liberia have won just one of their last eight matches (D2, L5), with that success coming in a 3-1 friendly victory over Sierra Leone in June, while they have scored just once in their two qualifiers, making a trip to Praia a difficult assignment for a side ranked 146th in the world.

The midfield options include Deroy Duarte, Kevin Pina, Jamiro Monteiro and Laros Duarte, while Dailon Livramento and Ryan Mendes are among the leading attacking options.

Huddersfield Town winger Derenseli Fernandes has been included, but defenders Roberto Lopes and Diney Borges are missing from the selection.

Liberia also have significant absentees, with captain Oscar Dorley ruled out after picking up a hamstring injury while playing for Saudi Arabian side Al-Taawoun.

Goalkeeper Tommy Songo is also injured, with Derrick Julu recalled to replace him.

Erradi has welcomed back Hammarby Talang striker William Gibson, while Ralph Weah has also earned a place in the 24-man squad.

#1942. Powers of recovery on show from Eastbourne Borough – now for double knockout test

On Tuesday night, the Sports swept away visitors Dulwich Hamlet 4-2 - and so moved swiftly on, after themselves conceding four goals on Saturday. So what went wrong at Dartford?

Boss Steve King addressed that: "That was the worst that we've played under me. We were all over the place defensively. There were individual mistakes and collective errors.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"We had our moments, had our chances - we hit the crossbar, hit the post. Josh Rees is about to score at the back post and he's having the shirt pulled off his back.

"But all in all, that first half performance was unacceptable. We chopped and changed a few things for the second half, but Dartford took their foot off the gas. You cannot concede four goals in a half of football."

Borough supporters - and many observers further afield - have frankly been raising their expectations week by week, as King's team chalked up the victories. But his post-match verdict was right on the money.

Firstly, Borough's defensive resources were stretched beyond the limit. And secondly, their errors were ruthlessly punished by an in-form Dartford. "There hasn't been another opponent that we've played who were as clinical as that.

"But listen, we've been on a heck of a run, fourteen wins out of fifteen. I said a few words, but nothing too strong. Pick yourselves up, and we go again!"

And go again they did: on a bleak Tuesday night, the Sports blew away visitors Dulwich Hamlet 4-2. With a relentless fixture schedule, King and his staff must manage resources.

At Dartford he had to field a centre-back pairing of full-back Elliott Johnson and the freshly returning Harry Phipps. And when Matthew Hayden - arguably the find of the season - chose the Dartford trip to have an off-day, the writing was on the dressing-room wall.

But with that game out of their systems, another three league points were in the kitty after Tuesday's victory.

King said of the Hamlet win: "At times we were very good. DIsappointed with the first Dulwich goal - it's a good finish but he's got in between our defenders. But then a good recovery from that with two excellent goals, from Josh (Rees) and Macca (Darren McQueen).

"At 3-1 I felt comfortable, but then we should have gone on to score more. Five, six, seven with the chances we were missing. At that point I actually said to Ryan (Northmore, assistant manager) - they're going to score again! And then it's going to be game on again!

"We were just woeful in our finishing! So that little period of the game wasn't great - and we've given Dulwich a leg up. But then Nashy Liam Nash) has scored and it's great to have him back!

"So it could have been much more comfortable. But when you lose a game (at Dartford) the question is - can you recover? And we have done that, and it's another win under the belt.

"The conditions were tough again with the wind and the rain - but it's another three points, and that's all you ever get for a victory. It's the most important thing. If you can get three points and play really well, that's even better. But the points are the first requirement.

"It was actually a tough night, because we've got some illness in the camp. And through the day we weren't quite sure who was ill and who had recovered, and who was fit and who was still injured.

"We were just counting the bodies. Gold (Omotayo) was ill and Terrell (Egbri) was ill. Elliott (Johnson) had a shoulder that swelled up. Fortunately we've had a good bench and so they all played their part. But it was a challenging day, with a lot of permutations!

Now Borough can turn their attention to a different competition - or two, in fact.

Tomorrow (Saturday) Chertsey Town visit the Connect Management Stadium in the FA Trophy. The Curfews play in the Southern League Premier South.

This Borough squad is full of seasoned professionals, and - in contrast to recent seasons - completely free of would-be superstars. They work hard, they know the system, and - most of all - they have brought a little bit of joy back. There is a cheerful connection with Borough's ever so slightly barmy army of supporters - who sang their hearts out, even in defeat, at Dartford.

King said: "Now we turn to Saturday, and Chertsey in the Trophy. Chertsey Town are a good side - they've beaten some strong opposition this season, and they've won again in midweek. So I'm expecting a very tough game.

"It's the Trophy of course, and a break from the league, which is actually welcome. And then another cup game next Tuesday (Littlehampton in the Sussex Senior Cup). So they are coming thick and fast - we will have had six weeks of Saturday-Tuesday-Saturday. I'm hoping by Saturday week to have players back and to be closer to a full squad - when we make the trip to Enfield for a really important league game!"

As King said, Tuesday sees yet another home fixture, the Sports welcoming Littlehampton Town in the Senior Cup.

Two seasons ago, the Marigolds muscled Borough out of a Senior Cup semi-final at Lancing. Revenge? Not exactly, but a chance to set the record straight, and score a few more goals. It's never goalless at the Lane.

#1940. Morocco vs Niger - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 11 Nov 2026 18:45

Morocco will be looking to maintain their perfect start to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they welcome Niger to the Mohammed V Stadium in Casablanca on Friday.

The Atlas Lions have collected six points from their opening two Group A matches and sit top of the table after beating Gabon and Lesotho, while the visitors are third with three points, having won one and lost one of their opening two qualifiers.

Morocco have made an impressive start to their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign, winning both of their opening Group A matches against Gabon and Lesotho by identical 2-0 scorelines.

The Atlas Lions have scored four goals without conceding in the qualifiers, underlining their defensive organisation, while they have now kept clean sheets in three of their last four competitive matches.

Mohamed Ouahbi's side have since returned to action, playing out a 1-1 friendly draw with Mali in October, with Abdessamad Ezzalzouli scoring from the penalty spot in the first half before Gaoussou Diarra restored parity for the opposition.

The hosts will be looking to maintain their defensive solidity in competitive matches, and their previous meetings with Niger offer plenty of encouragement, having won all six encounters between the sides while conceding just once.

Morocco have also been particularly solid defensively in recent AFCON qualifying campaigns, conceding just twice in six matches during the previous edition of the competition and keeping four clean sheets, while they have now recorded six shutouts in their last eight matches in the tournament's qualifiers.

Niger, meanwhile, have struggled to build on their encouraging start to the qualifying campaign, opening with a 2-1 victory over Lesotho before suffering a 2-0 defeat against Gabon.

The Menas followed that loss with another 2-0 defeat, this time against Algeria in a friendly last month, leaving them with three losses from their last four matches across all competitions.

Their victory over Lesotho remains their only triumph in their last nine matches, a run that has also produced five defeats and three draws.

Niger's away record makes this an even more difficult assignment, with the Menas losing two of their last four competitive matches on the road, including a 5-0 defeat against Morocco in a previous World Cup qualifier.

Sofyan Amrabat, Amine Harit and Amine Adli are also absent from the selection, while Youssef En-Nesyri has returned to the national team and Ayoub Oufkir has received his first senior call-up.

Neil El Aynaoui has also withdrawn after suffering an ankle problem during the international gathering, with Samir El Mourabet called up as his replacement.

#1938. Man United are a rotten, shambolic mess. They lack intelligence, look uncoached and fumbling, failing Michael Carrick is not the man to arrest this trauma, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 14:32 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 20:25 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United do not have a football team, more a collection of adrenaline junkies. Over time, it will not be enough.

So deficient are Michael Carrick's players that they surely can't keep their manager in a job for much longer. For the most part United are shambolic, a mess. At times they play football so devoid of intelligence and competence that it's almost impossible to fathom. They look uncoached.

Yet here they were for the second night running at Old Trafford, completing a lap of honour at full-time while their supporters sang the name of Carrick as he completed his own journey in front of the Stretford End towards the tunnel.

United – it's worth pointing out – are third bottom of the Premier League. They haven't won in the league since August and have conceded more goals across all competitions – 30 – than any team bar Crystal Palace in Europe's top divisions.

But at Old Trafford they will cling to anything to help them look in the mirror without laughing and currently the currency is comebacks. There was one against Roma in the Champions League last Tuesday and here – quite remarkably – there were two in one game.

None of it should really mean anything in the grand scheme. United are rotten, capable of playing effectively only when something gives them an energy spike with which to roll. It makes for quite hypnotic theatre but has inadequacy and desperation at its core.

Patrick Dorgu (centre) scored a late equaliser as troubled Man United drew 4-4 vs Aston Villa

Dorgu scored in the 96th-minute with this header but United sit 18th in the Premier League

Despite the draw, Michael Carrick's position as United head coach looks increasingly doubtful

It won't sustain them or indeed their fumbling, failing manager. But for the moment it's what they have and what they are.

MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Lammens 4; Mazraoui 4, Yoro 6, Maguire 5 (Heaven 46, 5), Dalot 3 (Dorgu 66, 8); Tielemans 6 (Mount 66, 5), Mainoo 6; Amad 5 (Lacey 66, 7), Fernandes 6, Cunha 7; Mbeumo 5 (Zirkzee 83, 7)

Goals: Fernandes (16 pen), Tielemans (44), Zirkzee (90+2), Dorgu (90+6)

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 5, Lindelof 6, Torres 6, Maatsen 4; Goretzka 6 (Mbaye 78, 6), Kamara 4; Alysson 7 (Barkley 71, 6), McGinn 8 (Hemmings 71, 6), Manzambi 6; Jackson 6 (Madjo 86)

Goals: Alysson (1), Jackson (4), McGinn (48 pen), Goretzka (53)

Here, they twice trailed by two, at the start of both halves. They were 2-0 down after only four minutes and 4-2 behind after 53. Somehow they managed not to lose.

The two goals United scored in added time at the end of the game came from absolutely nowhere. On the touchline Carrick – free from total humiliation for the second time in six days – raised a single finger to the sky.

In the directors' box – where the TV companies seem to have a camera permanently trained these days – fist pumps were in evidence from those in United blazers.

This was another uncomfortable afternoon for Messrs Ratcliffe, Wilcox and Berrada. A collection of new banners in the crowd made feelings known.

For now, Carrick is being spared any of the blame. That is strange and wrong but tells us much about the confused nature of the modern United. If they blame one of their own then they really do have nowhere left to go in search of self-respect.

United's opening against Roma last week had been traumatic enough. This was even worse but the root of it was desperately familiar – incompetent football.

The hapless United full-back Diogo Dalot was to blame for the first goal as Villa's Brazilian Alysson blasted his shot through the Portuguese's limp challenge. Later – after conceding a second half penalty – Dalot was booed off by his own fans.

That was painful and unedifying but completely understandable. Dalot has played more than 250 games for United yet has never even been good enough.

Aston Villa took the lead after just 59 seconds when Alysson (centre) scored at Old Trafford

Nicolas Jackson (centre) doubled the visitors' lead on four minutes as they made a dream start

Bruno Fernandes pulled one back for the hosts with a penalty on 16 minutes in a crazy start

For goal two, goalkeeper Senne Lammens was culpable as he pushed Alysson's shot into the path of Nicolas Jackson.

Once again United were in sink or swim territory. Once again, amazingly, they kept their heads above water – at least for a while.

Boubacar Kamara's 13th minute challenge on Matheus Cunha was stupid as the Brazilian was heading away from goal. But the Bruno Fernandes penalty that followed was calm and precise and the shot of belief United needed was theirs.

For the next 20 minutes or so, Carrick's team played well off the back of it. It was the only part of their game that will look good on the highlights. The United front four pressed and harried the Villa defence to the extent that Unai Emery's team couldn't get up the field.

Villa keeper Zion Suzuki saved well from a Cunha curler while subsequent shots from Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Amad Diallo took deflections and narrowly missed the target.

At some stage it felt as though United's energy must drop. Over time it did. But then they equalised.

Moments after seeing Suzuki save one of his own efforts, Amad found space to pull the ball back for Youri Tielemans who placed his first United goal in from 18 yards against his old club. Carrick's team deserved to be level at that stage and had played some enterprising football to get there. But their self-harm gene surfaced again before long.

Youri Tielemans (right) brought United level before half-time with this strike vs his old club

John McGinn put Villa ahead again just minutes after half-time from the penalty spot

Leon Goretkza (left) made it 4-2 to Villa with this close-range strike as they looked set to win

Joshua Zirkzee (left) pulled one back in second-half stoppage-time with this finish for United

Alysson had almost scored with the last big moment of the first half and in the 47th minute he drew an utterly dumb foul from Dalot and John McGinn scored the penalty firmly.

United are beyond compare in the Premier League when it comes to this kind of thing. Who else in the top flight concedes the kind of goals they do? A case in point came in the 53rd minute.

McGinn's free-kick was heading across goal and away when United defender Leny Yoro inexplicably headed it towards his own goal. Lammens somehow touched the ball on to the bar but when it dropped Leon Goretzka poked it in.

That was the 16th goal United had conceded in the last five games and this time the attempt at a fightback was more muted.

There were some half chances – shots from Cunha and Fernandes – and some territory in which to play.

But this was a game Villa were now able to control rather better and they looked set to ease home until Patrick Dorgu crossed for Joshua Zirkzee to ease a goal in from out of nothing in the 2nd minute of added time.

Old Trafford was emptying fast by the time Dorgu headed in a 96th equaliser from a corner. But by then the collective blood was up once more and it was enough.

Villa appealed for a foul on goalkeeper Suzuki and it's true Lammens had gone looking for him. Was the contact between the two 'keepers significant enough to warrant VAR intervention? Probably not. United had their draw and they had a point.

If the season ended today, they would be down. Yet they were cheered off. Some things you just can't make up.

#1935. Arsenal battle Real Madrid and PSG for £44m-rated Borussia Dortmund wonderkid

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 20:07, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 20:08

Arsenal are reportedly among three European heavyweights monitoring Borussia Dortmund defender Joane Gadou, with Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain also interested in the highly rated French teenager.

The 19-year-old has quickly established himself in the Bundesliga following his summer move from Red Bull Salzburg, attracting attention from some of Europe's biggest clubs after an impressive start to his Dortmund career.

According to German outlet Fussball News, citing transfer journalist Ekrem Konur, Arsenal, Real Madrid and PSG have been following Gadou's development closely and have sent scouts to watch him in action.

Dortmund are reluctant to lose the defender just months after signing him, although offers in the region of €40m to €50m (£35m to £44m) could reportedly persuade the German club to reconsider their position.

No formal asking price has been announced, and there is currently no indication that any of the interested clubs have submitted an offer.

A January transfer is considered highly unlikely, with the summer of 2027 potentially providing a more realistic opportunity for the player's admirers.

Gadou has made a rapid impression at Dortmund, having started 12 of his 15 appearances across all competitions during the opening months of the 2026-27 campaign.

The Frenchman has become a regular member of Niko Kovac's defensive unit, competing alongside established players such as Nico Schlotterbeck and Waldemar Anton.

Standing at 1.95 metres, Gadou combines an imposing physical presence with considerable pace and an ability to contribute to his team's build-up play.

His versatility has also been evident, with the teenager capable of operating on the right of a back three or filling in at right-back when required.

Those qualities have reportedly attracted scouts from Arsenal, Real Madrid and PSG, who are understood to have watched him during Dortmund's encounters with Real Betis and Bayern Munich.

For Arsenal, Gadou is already a familiar opponent.

The defender scored against the Gunners during the Emirates Cup in August, finding the net in the second half as Dortmund secured a 3-2 pre-season victory in north London.

That appearance provided an early opportunity for the Premier League champions to assess the youngster at close quarters, although there is no evidence that it directly prompted their reported transfer interest.

Gadou's development has been particularly rapid considering that he was still part of PSG's academy little more than two years ago.

He left the French champions for Salzburg in September 2024 without making a senior appearance in Paris, subsequently establishing himself in Austria before earning a move to Dortmund in May 2026.

The Bundesliga club reportedly paid approximately €19.5m (£17m) for his services, with further bonuses potentially increasing the overall fee.

Dortmund's sporting director Lars Ricken made clear at the time that the club had followed Gadou since his PSG days and expected him to play an important role immediately.

The French youth international has justified that confidence with his early performances, and his progress now appears to have attracted renewed attention from his former club.

Despite the growing interest, Dortmund are under no immediate pressure to negotiate Gadou's departure.

The defender signed a five-year contract upon his arrival from Salzburg, keeping him at Signal Iduna Park until June 2031.

That long-term agreement places the German club in a strong position should Arsenal, Real Madrid or PSG decide to formalise their interest.

According to Fussball News, bids approaching €40m to €50m could be required before Dortmund would consider changing their stance.

However, that figure represents a reported potential negotiating range rather than an official valuation communicated by the club.

Gadou's estimated market value currently stands at approximately €28m (£24.5m), highlighting the premium Dortmund could seek for a player who has already established himself in their first-team plans.

The Bundesliga side are also understood to have little appetite for selling the Frenchman during the January transfer window.

For PSG, a future move would represent an opportunity to bring back a player developed in their academy, although they would now face a substantial financial commitment to secure his return.

Arsenal and Real Madrid, meanwhile, are being linked with a defender whose early performances suggest that his reputation could continue to grow before next summer.

Much will depend on whether any of the three clubs progress beyond their reported scouting interest.

For now, Gadou remains an important part of Dortmund's plans, and his lengthy contract gives the German side considerable control over any potential transfer negotiations.

#1934. Simon Leslie: We wanted an Eastbourne Borough response – and got it in style under the lights

On another afternoon it could have finished 6-1 to Borough, but they scored four from five shots on target and we managed one from ten. Sometimes football leaves you wondering how on earth you have lost a game like that.

Our fans, however, were amazing. You sang and sang, even when there was no way back. When you have travelled to support your team and the afternoon goes against you, that takes some doing. Thank you.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

I did wonder whether the manager of the month curse had struck again! Congratulations to Steve King on his thoroughly deserved award. One difficult afternoon certainly doesn’t undo the work that earned it.

What mattered next was how the boys responded, and Tuesday evening against Dulwich Hamlet gave us plenty to be proud of.

Conceding in the second minute was hardly the start we wanted. After Saturday, it would have been easy for heads to drop. Instead, these boys worked their socks off and went into half-time 3-1 up.

The second half was harder going in the rain, but the boys stuck at it and came away with a 4-2 win. A proper response to Saturday and three very welcome points, especially as Welling dropped a couple of points down the road.

Bobby, our commentator, and I both had Liam Nash as our man of the match. Considering he has been out for so many weeks, he was amazing. It was lovely to see him back playing so well.

It was bitterly cold, too. To everyone who came out, wrapped up and got behind the team, thank you. There are certainly warmer ways to spend a Tuesday evening, and we appreciate you choosing to spend yours with us.

Tomorrow is a huge occasion as Chertsey Town visit for an FA Trophy second round tie. I would love to see a big crowd at Priory Lane helping the boys take another step in the competition. Bring a friend, bring the family and bring your voices. A few extra layers might be sensible as well!

We have also had another trophy to celebrate. Our Spirit of Football team recently paraded their first silverware in front of a packed stadium, and we are so proud of every one of them. Seeing the reception they received was a lovely moment for everyone involved.

As the weather gets more miserable, there is plenty happening indoors at the club. Padel is great fun for all ages, good exercise and, judging by everyone who has tried it, highly addictive. Come down and give it a go.

Our new simulators also let you play golf at thousands of courses, with all the excitement and no wet clothes afterwards. Both the Padel Centre and Simulator Centre make great Christmas party venues, whether you are getting together with friends, family or work colleagues.

For now, though, let’s get behind the boys tomorrow and make it another cup afternoon to remember.

#1933. Bulgaria vs Iceland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 20:37

Iceland could clinch promotion to Nations League C by beating hosts Bulgaria on Friday at Stadion Hristo Botev.

The Icelandic national team are currently top of Group C with eight points from four matchdays, whereas their opponents are third with four points and must win if they are to make certain that they remain in the race for promotion.

Given six games will take place in the group, Bulgaria would be unable to catch Iceland if they were to take just a point on Friday, but a win for second-placed Estonia against Luxembourg on the same day would increase their points tally to nine and make them unreachable.

Unfortunately for boss Atanas Ribarski, his side have only won one of their last six games in all competitions, losing on three occasions.

The hosts did beat Luxembourg 2-0 on October 6 in their most recent Nations League outing, and that was their second clean sheet in the group stage.

At the other end of the pitch, the Lions have only scored three goals in this iteration of the competition, and they have failed to find the back of the net in eight of their 15 most recent games.

Bulgaria have lost five of their past 10 clashes at home, a stretch in which they triumphed just once and were held to four stalemates.

Only first place will guarantee progression into Nations League B, and Iceland would secure first if they beat Bulgaria and Estonia lost against Luxembourg.

Head coach Arnar Gunnlaugsson will be frustrated that his side failed to beat Estonia on October 6, when the two sides drew 0-0.

However, Strakarnir Okkar are unbeaten in four games, winning twice, though it may be a concern that they have only won two of their past 10 clashes.

The visitors managed to beat their hosts 3-0 when they met on October 3, winning for the first time in any of their five encounters, with Bulgaria claiming victory three times.

Iceland come into Friday's match having drawn one and won one of their two away fixtures in the Nations League so far, but they were winless in their prior six contests on the road, suffering four defeats.

Bulgaria must be careful to avoid needless yellow cards on Friday given eight players are at risk of picking up a suspension, though they know they will be able to welcome back goalkeeper Dimitar Mitov and winger Lukas Petkov.

Mitov is likely to be stationed behind a back four featuring centre-backs Stefan Velkov and Emil Tsenov, while Andrian Kraev and Ilia Gruev could start in a double pivot.

Petkov is set to start on the right side of attack, with Kristiyan Balov on the left flank and Atanas Iliev through the middle.

Iceland could position Andri Gudjohnsen in an advanced role behind striker Orri Oskarsson, with the pair likely to be supported by midfielders Gylfi Sigurdsson and Isak Bergmann Johannesson.

Central defenders Brynjar Ingi Bjarnason and Hordur Magnusson are candidates to start in the heart of a back four.

Mitov; Stoyanov, Velkov, Tsenov, Petrov; Kraev, Gruev; Petkov, Rusev, Balov; Iliev

Valdimarsson; Palsson, Bjarnason, Magnusson, Gretarsson; Sigurdsson, Johannesson; Haraldsson, Gudjohnsen, Anderson; Oskarsson

Though home advantage has often been crucial for many teams, Bulgaria have struggled for consistency when playing as hosts.

Iceland have also performed well on their travels in the Nations League, and they should be confident that they can take three points on Friday.

#1932. Sebastien Pocognoli must take next Scotland step - especially with two key reinforcements

There was a certain amount of grace afforded to Sebastien Pocognoli’s first international break as Scotland manager.

Back in September/October, Scotland played four Nations League B1 matches across three weeks - defeating North Macedonia in Skopje, drawing with Slovenia in Ljubljana and losing at home to Switzerland and the Slovenians.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A new voice, a new style and some new players. Debuts were given to defenders Stephen Welsh, Luis Binks, Luke Graham, winger Josh McPake and striker Robbie Ure. The likes of Oli McBurnie returned. A fresh formation was implemented. Pocognoli’s Scotland looked very different to his predecessor, Steve Clarke.

The change has largely been welcomed amid criticism of a stale style under Clarke. And up until the visit of Slovenia in the final match of the quartet, there was optimism that Scotland were going in the right direction. The 2-1 reversal by the visitors, however, leaves Scotland in an unenviable position in this group. Finishing second is the best Pocognoli can hope for, and that would require at the very least taking four points from North Macedonia and Switzerland in the final two matches.

Last time out, four points on the road was pleasing. The 3-0 defeat by Switzerland - World Cup quarter-finalists, it must be stressed - could be partly explained by an early red card for Jack Hendry. The performance against Slovenia at home raised concerns, though, with Scotland too open, fatigued and meek in the final third.

Pocognoli knows that at the very least in this international fortnight, Scotland must beat North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday. The Balkan nation are toiling, have not taken a point so far and looked bedraggled when Scotland vanquished them. It would breathe some confidence into the team ahead of Monday’s trip to St Gallen, where Scotland will face a Swiss side that may already have top spot sewn up.

Finishing second would require positive results in both fixtures. Doing so would be significant, as it would make Scotland second seeds in next month’s Euro 2028 qualification draw.

What is more feasible is improvement from Scotland. While the team certainly played with more adventure and gumption, there remained a lack of ruthlessness in the final third. Kieron Bowie scored his first goal for his country, but McBurnie remains strike-less after 20 appearances. Perhaps the North Macedonians will be more accommodating.

Pocognoli is able to replenish his forward line with two important members of the Scotland squad for the past few years. Torino striker Che Adams missed out last time due to a muscle injury, but he is fit and firing in Serie A, having scored four goals this season. Often asked to plough a lone furrow under Clarke, it will be fascinating to see how he thrives in a more forward-thinking set-up - and potentially with a partner up top.

Adams’ return is welcomed but there can be no doubt that Pocognoli will be most excited to work with Scott McTominay. The 29-year-old talisman was ruled out of the first camp with a minor heart issue but after a successful operation, he has returned to Napoli and while Gli Azzurri are toiling in mid-table, McTominay has netted five goals and remains front and centre of their best work.

Competition in the midfield area remains fierce. Shoehorning McTominay, John McGinn, Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson and Ryan Christie into one team has always been a challenge and will be even harder if Pocognoli decides to stick with two strikers - which he should do against opposition of North Macedonia’s calibre. A combination of Adams and McBurnie in attack seems likely, especially as Bowie has not been starting regularly for Sassuolo.

Gilmour became front and centre of Scotland’s midfield in the last international window and was Scotland’s main source of vertical creativity. McGinn and Ferguson started every game - and both are in good form with their clubs. At Bologna, Ferguson tops the charts in Serie A for distance covered (114.1m), total passes (817) and accurate passes (754). Christie and Bournemouth are flying. These are nice problems to have.

Scotland looked jaded by the second match against Slovenia and while this break is shorter, there is an argument for more rotation. And there will have to be changes in defence, given Welsh and Binks have been forced to withdraw from this squad, replaced by forgotten men Ryan Porteous and David Bates, while Scott McKenna is also absent.

Pocognoli operated with a back three but may be minded to change given the absentees and porousness against stronger opposition. While Porteous has fared well in the States with LA, Graham - often a starter for Stoke City - may be ahead of him in the international pecking order. Kieran Tierney withdrew from the last squad, but is fit this time around and can play as a left-sided centre-half.

Captain Andy Robertson will move level with Sir Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps should he be, as is expected, deployed on the left flank. There is more debate on the other side. Winger Ben Gannon-Doak could give Scotland more oomph in a game they have to win than Aaron Hickey and Nathan Patterson.

There’s even debate with the goalkeeper. Angus Gunn’s status as an untouchable No 1 waned a little on the back of performances last month. Could in-form Falkirk stopper Scott Bain oust him?

Pocognoli has options, that’s for sure. The Tartan Army will want to see Scotland more secure tactically. There needs to be a step forward in this brave new world. And while winning in Switzerland may prove a step too far, landing a first home win under the 39-year-old Belgian feels non-negotiable.

North Macedonia at home was the sort of match Scotland gobbled up in the past. This may be a new regime, but that particular old habit must die hard.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Pietro Terracciano, Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Alexis Saelemaekers, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Samuel Chukwueze and Strahinja Pavlovic were all out for the match at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris, with the Serbian centre-back being the latest to enter the treatment room.

“This is essentially a message to the owners, who have already promised to intervene in the January transfer window to fill the gaps. The point is precisely this: until then, the Portuguese coach must continue with his current strength.

Handing international debuts to no less than five players in his maiden camp as Scotland head coach, the Belgian boss has shown no fear when it comes to introducing fresh faces to his pack. However, he came under scrutiny for his willingness to adopt a back three formation, with many pundits questioning whether the team has the personnel to adapt.

Curious to see what he has learned from last month’s games, 50-cap former Scotland international Alan Hutton thinks it will take time for the team to adapt to his methods, but would like to see improved performances against North Macedonia and Switzerland over the next week as the team return to action.

“Taking the four games Pocognoli has had, he's just come into the job, so a lot of information has been passed down to the players,” said Hutton. “Even with an extended break, which he would have appreciated, it's very difficult to get concepts across in such a short period of time. He'll be looking to develop that and reinforce his tactical ideas. Hopefully, they digest it better going into these two games.

“They beat North Macedonia away, so you'd hope he can get his first win at home to put that to bed. Switzerland away is going to be difficult, but you want to see progression in how they understand his philosophy on the pitch. It's still very early in his tenure and he's going to be given time to get it right. He's refreshed the squad with younger faces, and they need time to adapt as well, so while it has to improve, it requires patience.”

One of the main points of contention has been Scotland’s inability to finish chances that come their way. With Kieron Bowie the only striker to get on the scoresheet last month, questions have been asked about who should get the nod to lead the forward line in the upcoming games. Hutton believes one man has the number nine shirt - for now, at least.

“I know it's been an issue,” Hutton told OLBG. “Even going back to when I was playing, and that's no slight on anyone who played, but we lacked a guy who guarantees goals. Everything has been workmanlike, working hard and holding the ball up, but you need someone to put the ball in the back of the net.

“I think [Oli} McBurnie is the go-to guy at this moment. I really like Kieron Bowie and Robbie Ure, they're young and they will get better in the leagues they're in, improving technically and in their hold-up play. McBurnie is the main man right now, though the others will be breathing down his neck.”

#1928. Mali vs Rwanda - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 11 Nov 2026 23:07, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 18:01

Mali host Rwanda at the Stade du 26 Mars in Bamako on Friday, November 13, in the third round of Group K in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, with kickoff at 19:00 GMT.

Both sides won their opening two games and sit on six points with a goal difference of +3, Rwanda ahead on goals scored (five to four), and only the top two in a group with no host nation reach the finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

Anthony Da Silva's first competitive game in charge of Les Aigles ended in a 3-1 home win over Cape Verde, a side who played at this summer's World Cup, on September 25.

Ange Martial Tia scored after five minutes, Sidny Cabral equalised in the 10th minute, and Nene Dorgeles then scored in the 39th and 51st minutes.

Tia also scored the only goal in Paynesville on September 29, in the 79th minute, after which Da Silva said Liberia had defended well on a synthetic pitch.

A 1-1 friendly draw with Morocco in Tangier on October 4, in which Gaoussou Diarra cancelled out Abdessamad Ezzalzouli's 35th-minute penalty in the 77th minute, leaves Mali unbeaten in their last three games.

Mali have never lost to Rwanda, winning three and drawing one of four World Cup qualifiers, with a 7-2 aggregate goal record.

The latest two meetings were a 1-0 home win on September 1, 2021 and a 3-0 win in Kigali on November 11, 2021, yet Da Silva has still described the chances of the two teams as equal.

The Amavubi began with a 3-1 win over Liberia in Kigali on September 25, with Abeddy Biramahire scoring in the second minute, Leroy Mickels in the 33rd and Joy-Lance Mickels from the penalty spot in the 44th.

In Praia on September 29 they trailed to Gilson Benchimol's 40th-minute goal, before Claude Niyomugabo equalised in first-half stoppage time with a long-range strike from a corner.

Elie Tatou Iradukunda scored the winner in the 52nd minute after a mistake by Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, and Rwanda were outshot 19-6 over the 90 minutes.

Stephen Constantine, in his second spell as Rwanda coach, declared after that win that "the revolution has begun", and his side also drew 0-0 with Kenya on October 5 in an international friendly match in Kigali.

Rwanda are chasing a first AFCON finals appearance since 2004, and Constantine has said he will take one game at a time while rating Group K as containing two of the better teams in Africa.

They have never beaten Mali, scoring only two goals in four meetings, and have conceded in both qualifiers so far.

Rwanda Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Tia, who has scored twice in two caps for Mali, is out with an ankle injury, while Adama Camara (hamstring) and Lassana Coulibaly (biceps femoris) are also unavailable.

West Ham midfielder Mohamadou Kante receives his first call-up after choosing Mali over France and Senegal, and Swansea City winger Moussa Yeo, 22, is also new after scoring three times in his last five club games.

Gaoussou Diakite of Red Bull Salzburg and Fode Doucoure of Nantes return in a 24-man squad that does not include Yves Bissouma, who joined Ajax in late September, with no reason given for his absence.

For the visitors, Constantine trimmed his squad on Monday, November 9, dropping Elie Ganijuru, Kevin Muhire, Taiba Mbonyumwami and goalkeeper Yves Mugisha, while Fidele Uwiyaremye had already been sent home on the first day of camp for disciplinary reasons.

Defender Thierry Manzi and midfielder Jean Bosco Ruboneka are back after missing the September qualifiers, and Bonheur Mugisha, Gilbert Mugisha and Leroy-Jacques Mickels joined the camp on Monday.

Rwanda's winner in Praia came from a goalkeeping error and they were outshot 19-6 there, while Mali have conceded only Cabral's goal in two games, so chances should be scarce for the Amavubi in Bamako.

Tia's absence removes the scorer of two of Mali's four goals, which is why a narrow margin looks more likely than a repeat of the 3-0 in Kigali in 2021.

Rwanda have scored more than Mali, and with the return leg in Kigali on November 17 a draw in Bamako would suit them.

#1926. Inside big Andy Robertson decision as Scotland landmark brings Liverpool legend comeback quip

Andy Robertson stands on the brink of making international history in the coming days as he prepares to move level with Sir Kenny Dalglish’s appearance record for Scotland.

The Tottenham full-back is closing in on a significant career milestone that would see him match Dalglish on 102 caps for his country should he feature in Friday’s UEFA Nations League clash against North Macedonia at Hampden, underlining his importance to the team over the past decade.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Since making his senior international debut back in 2014, the 32-year-old has gone to captain his nation and help guide Scotland to successive European Championship tournaments.

His longevity and consistency at the highest level have made him a central figure in the national team, with former Scotland manager Alex McLeish among those who have witnessed first-hand the qualities that make Robertson such an important leader.

McLeish handed Robertson the armband in 2018 and believes his standing in the Premier League, alongside his personality and popularity within the dressing room, made his decision a straightforward one as he paid a glowing tribute to the defender.

“He's been an amazing servant for club and country,” McLeish declared just over a month on from presenting Robertson with a framed shirt to commemorate earning his 100th cap. “Andy's obviously on the verge of equalling Kenny's caps record so maybe Kenny will need to make a comeback! No, seriously Andy is still doing the country proud and it's great to see.

“When I made him captain it felt like natural progress. I just felt that his stature, as a player at Liverpool, playing at the level he was playing at, made him the ideal man. He has a real passion for the game and he's also super popular with the other players. They all respect him and look up to him.”

Moving level with Dalglish’s tally in the all-time charts would represent another major landmark in a career that has seen Robertson become one of the most successful Scottish footballers of his generation and cement his place among the country's greatest ever servants.

Meanwhile, another former Scotland boss, Craig Levein, has urged patience when assessing the early stages of Sebastien Pocognoli's tenure, suggesting it remains too soon to make firm judgements about the new head coach.

With Scotland entering a new chapter following Steve Clarke's time in charge, Levein believes there will inevitably be a transition period under the Belgian as some of the more experienced heads approach the latter stages of their international careers.

“It's too early to tell, isn't it? At some point, some of these players who are getting on a little bit are going to be getting into the point where they would probably be coming off the bench and then maybe disappearing from the squads altogether,” Levein admitted.

“Steve did an unbelievable job in getting Scotland to these tournaments. I do think that he had probably the best squad of players that Scotland had for a long, long time. Those two things merged very well, and they did a fantastic job.

“I don't know much about the new guy at all. I haven't really needed to do any research like you guys have. So we'll just have to give the guy time and wait and see what happens.”

#1925. Slovakia vs Faroe Islands - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 23:07, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 05:09

Kosicka Futbalova Arena will be the backdrop for a crucial showdown between two unbeaten teams in UEFA Nations League C's Group 3 on Friday, when Slovakia host Faroe Islands.

The Falcons could earn a fourth win in five games, though Landslidid will be motivated by the possibility of promotion.

Vladimir Weiss's Slovakia have produced an impressive campaign in the Nations League, and head into this week's showdown on the cusp of ascension to League B.

The Falcons kicked off their group action with a 2-0 win over Moldova on September 26, which they followed up three days later by beating Kazakhstan 2-1, making it six points from six on home turf.

Weiss's side also hammered Moldova 4-0 in their most recent outing on October 6, though they were held to a 1-1 draw by Friday's opponents prior - the only match the country have failed to triumph in so far.

Ten points from four games have put Slovakia in a commanding position at the top of Nations League Group C3, six clear of second-placed Faroe Islands.

Additionally, the Falcons - who have won four of their last five when playing as the hosts - know that even a draw would be enough to see them secure promotion with room to spare.

Meanwhile, Eydun Klakstein's Faroe Islands may be ranked 126th in the world by FIFA compared to Slovakia's 46th, but they will be cautiously optimistic ahead of this clash.

Landslidid are widely known as international strugglers, but they arrive on the back of a five-game unbeaten run, having yet to taste defeat in this edition of the Nations League.

That remarkable feat has Klakstein's men second in the table, sat in the promotion playoff spot and eyeing an improbable rise through the divisions.

On the other hand, it is notable that Faroe Islands have not come out on top in any of their four Nations League contests so far, even if they remain undefeated, drawing 2-2 with Kazakhstan last time out.

Likewise, Friday's visitors are level on four points with third-placed Moldova, who could usurp them given they are set to face bottom-of-the-pile Kazakhstan.

Slovakia will be lighter in midfield than ideal without Stanislav Lobotka (ankle) and the versatile Tomas Suslov (hamstring), though Peter Pokorny could be joined by Tomas Rigo and Ondrej Duda in the centre of the park.

Further forward, Middlesbrough's David Strelec may lead the attack, supported from out wide by Tomas Bobcek and Lukas Haraslin.

As for Faroe Islands, they are missing Mjallby left wing-back Martin Agnarsson, who is suspended after being sent off against Kazakhstan.

Filling the gaps this week, Klakstein could opt for Samuel Johansen Chukwudi on the left flank, with Joannes Kalso Danielsen on the right.

Elsewhere, Petur Knudsen should be on hand to start up top, supplied by Aki Samuelsen and Hanus Sorensen.

Greif; Mesik, Skriniar, Obert, Hancko; Rigo, Pokorny, Duda; Bobcek, Strelec, Haraslin

Lamhauge; Faero, Vatnhamar, Edmundsson; Danielsen, Turi, Bjartalid, Chukwudi; Samuelsen, Knudsen, Sorensen

Slovakia are the favourites owing to the superior quality in their squad, and their 81-better FIFA ranking, though they are unlikely to pull off a second consecutive thrashing.

Faroe Islands are the only nation that have caused the Falcons to drop points in Group C3, so expect to see another close-fought contest between two unbeaten sides.

Sebastien Pocognoli begins his second international break as Scotland head coach against North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday.

The Nations League fixture will provide the Belgian with a chance to claim his first home victory at the third attempt after the disappointing defeats by Switzerland and Slovenia last month.

North Macedonia meanwhile are searching for a sharp turnaround after losing five consecutive matches and failing to score in their last eight games, including the 2-0 defeat by Scotland in Skopje last month.

Pocognoli has endured an underwhelming start to his Scotland tenure, collecting just four points from his opening four games to leave his side third in Nations League Group B1 and facing an uphill task to finish in the top two.

Switzerland top the table on the maximum 12 points meaning Scotland are no longer able to overtake them or secure automatic promotion to Nations League A. A runners-up finish is still possible, which would secure a promotion play-off against a team who finishes second bottom of a Group A section, but would require Scotland to overhaul Slovenia, who are three points ahead in second place in the table.

A top two finish in Group B1 is also required for Scotland to guarantee second seed status for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, which takes place on December 6. Otherwise, Scotland are almost certain to be a pot three team.

Because the Slovenians hold the head-to-head advantage, Scotland must finish ahead of them on points to overtake them. Slovenia host Switzerland on Friday before travelling to Skopje to face North Macedonia on Monday. A victory in either match will clinch second place for them.

After Scotland host North Macedonia on Friday they travel to St. Gallen to face Switzerland on Monday. Pocognoli’s men will need four points if Slovenia lose both matches, but will need the maximum six points if Slovenia pick up one or two points.

The Nations League Group B1 fixture between Scotland and North Macedonia takes place at Hampden Park, Glasgow, on Friday, November 13, 2026. Kick-off is 7.45pm.

The match will be broadcast live on BBC2 and the BBC Scotland channel with coverage starting at 7.30pm.

The match will be available to live stream on the BBC Sport website and the BBC iPlayer.

Sebastien Pocognoli has been boosted by the return from injury of Kieran Tierney, Scott McTominay and Che Adams with the trio all in contention to start. However, the Scotland head coach has suffered a triple blow in defence, losing three centre-backs who started for him last month with the withdrawals of Stephen Welsh and Luis Binks adding to the absence of Scott McKenna from the original squad.

UEFA has assigned an Austrian pairing to the VAR booth. Alan Kijas will act as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) for the fixture, while Harald Lechner will support him as the Assistant Video Assistant Referee (AVAR).

Horsham have already faced the Gulls this season, drawing 1-1 at Plainmoor on the opening day of the 2026-27 campaign.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Di Paola admitted the Hornets couldn’t have asked for a tougher draw – but the boss hoped a little bit of luck could help Horsham progress.

He told us: “We said when it was drawn it was a tough one but we will approach like we have with every game. We’ll approach it with the right frame of mind.

“I’m desperate to get through. You only have to look at Plymouth Parkway [in the FA Cup] and the draws they’ve had in every round. That’s what you need. I’m not one to blow my own trumpet, but when you do well you do have a bit of luck.

“I’ll always remember the Woking game that got us our first first round [FA Cup appearance in 2021]. They had two or three great chances, Sam Howes made a great save, they missed one at the back post they should have scored, and then with a few minutes to go we scored a free kick that got us into the first round.

“You do need a bit of luck and Plymouth have had a lot of it in terms of draws. They’ve been at home every round – but that’s what you get sometimes. That’s cup football.

“We want to do well in the Trophy like we did last year – it’s good for the finances – but we’re coming up against a team that should make the play-offs comfortably, given the resources they’ve got.

“It’s not an ideal draw but what draw ever is? We would have said Plymouth Parkway was a good draw because they were in the league below, but obviously they were a good side.”

Jimmy Wild is cup-tied for the Trophy tie with Torquay, but the Hornets have no fresh injury concerns.

One player who will no longer feature for Horsham is Archy Taylor, who departed the club on Friday (November 6).

The full-back joined the Hornets ahead of the current season and made a total of 10 appearances.

On Taylor’s departure, Di Paola said: “It’s just unfortunate he’s come up against Lee Harding, who’s one of our best players. He just couldn’t get a foothold in the side.

“With Coxy [George Cox] coming in we have to balance the books, which is perfectly fair. It just got to the point where he wasn’t playing a lot.

“He’s only 22 and he’s probably had two years of setbacks and he just needs to play somewhere and get some football under his belt and get his confidence back. His confidence had gone through the floor because he wasn’t playing, which is common in footballers. He just needs to go and play and enjoy his football somewhere.

“He’s a lovely lad. He saw the writing on the wall and I respect anyone who wants to go and play football. I hate players who are quite happy to sit on the bench or not play.

“Especially younger players, I think money shouldn’t be a factor in your football life when you’re a kid. You should just want to get out and play football while you can because you’re a long time. Fair play to him for wanting to do that. All the best to him.”

Liverpool could finalise a new contract for Trey Nyoni in the international break, the latest report has claimed,

The unfortunate reality is that playing the 19-year-old every week could be dangerous as the risk of injury would increase significantly.

The report from GIVEMESPORT also states that there is currently no contract on the table for midfielder Alexis Mac Allister.

#1917. Tottenham wonderkid and £16m Everton star on Scotland radar as Sebastien Pocognoli confirms approach

Sebastien Pocognoli has revealed he has made approaches to Tottenham youngster Archie Gray and Everton midfielder Hayden Hackney about representing Scotland as he looks to strengthen his international options.

The Belgian head coach is determined to identify talented players with Scottish connections who could potentially represent the national team, and has confirmed that both Premier League prospects feature on his recruitment radar.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Gray and Hackney have represented England at youth level but are eligible to play for Scotland, although neither has committed to switching their international allegiance. Pocognoli admits he has already established contact with the pair but insists any decision will ultimately have to come from the players themselves.

His predecessor, Steve Clarke, previously attempted to persuade the likes of Elliot Anderson and Harvey Barnes to represent Scotland, without success. However, the country has enjoyed greater luck in other cases, with Scott McTominay and Che Adams going on to become influential figures after opting to play for the Tartan Army.

Pocognoli is currently satisfied with the depth available to him as Scotland prepare for their final Nations League fixtures against North Macedonia and Switzerland. Nevertheless, he believes expanding the pool of eligible talent must remain an ongoing priority.

Speaking about his efforts to identify potential recruits, Pocognoli said: “I am busy with everything. We know which players are eligible to represent the country one day. It’s won't come from me, it has to come from them to show it. I try to anticipate everything. The best way is to be proactive and creative in certain situations.

“The depth of the squad is already big without these other names. I’m very happy with it because we have a good double-up and triple-up in each position. But it’s part of my role, for sure [to find players]. Not only for me but for other people working at the Scottish FA. We are on it. We also have a lot of good players in the Under-21s and that’s the first step for me, for the future.

“But yeah, I have had direct or indirect contact (with Gray and Hackney). When I go to the direct contact it’s because I feel it’s a first positive approach. So yeah, I’ve done it with many players. I’ll do my best to bring them.”

Gray and Hackney have different international backgrounds, with Pocognoli acknowledging that any potential switch would require patience.

Gray, the son of former Scotland striker Andy Gray, also has family links to Scottish football through Leeds United legends Frank and Eddie Gray, both of whom represented the national side. The Tottenham midfielder has featured for England at every youth level but has yet to make his senior debut.

Hackney, meanwhile, previously represented Scotland at Under-21 level before switching his international allegiance to England.

Pocognoli believes the age of the two players makes them particularly interesting prospects but insists there is no immediate pressure for either to make a decision.

“With Barnes it was different. I knew before my first camp that he was different,” he said. “The two other lads [Gray and Hackney] are young lads. It’s a long way [away]. But if you wait too long, it might not be the right moment. In a year’s time, we will see. Right now, we have players in the squad who are performing well.

“It will always be up to them [current players] to be the priority, because we’ve built things and we’ve had time with the ones who are here right now. But we are on it. We are always proactive in all of these situations. What is very exciting about those two names is that they are young players.

“That’s interesting. We have to look and manage the situation. But it won’t be a definitive choice from them - because we weren’t proactive. That has to be clear. We are proactive.

“The best way to convince players is to show good football, show them they can come to us, enjoy it and be successful. They have to feel when they leave a top club that they arrive here into top conditions and a top environment.

“That’s the best publicity we can offer, to show good football. Yeah [McTominay is an example] but there are many.”

#1915. Burkina Faso vs Mauritania - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 11 Nov 2026 23:36, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 23:36

Burkina Faso will look to make it consecutive Africa Cup of Nations qualifying victories when Mauritania visit Stade du 4-Aout on Friday.

The teams are separated by just one point in a tightly packed Group F, with either side capable of ending matchday three at the summit.

Burkina Faso's consistency at the Africa Cup of Nations has soared in recent years, with eight appearances in the last nine tournaments after missing out in 2008 and 2010.

A 1-1 home draw with Benin and a 1-0 away win over the Central African Republic in their opening two qualifiers have put Moussa Sanogo’s side on course for another AFCON appearance, having collected four points from a possible six.

However, Les Etalons will need to bounce back from a 7-0 friendly defeat to Argentina in October, their joint-heaviest loss, matched only by a similar drubbing against Algeria in 1981.

Back on home turf, where they have not lost a competitive match in nearly a decade, Burkina Faso now aim to move to the top of their qualifying group with a win, or at least keep pace with Benin, who currently lead on goal difference.

Having beaten Mauritania in each of the last three meetings - including most recently in the 2024 Africa Cup of Nations group stage - Friday’s hosts will hope their psychological edge in this fixture aids their quest for maximum points and back-to-back competitive wins for the first time since December 2025.

Mauritania have not lost an opening AFCON qualifier since 2015, and they extended that streak with a 1-0 victory over the Central African Republic at Stade Larbi Zaouli in September. However, a 2-1 defeat to Benin in their next outing snapped their three-match unbeaten run.

Aritz Lopez Garai’s transition from the Under-20s to the senior side has been far from smooth. As the 46-year-old prepares for his 20th match in charge, he has recorded just five victories, giving him a win percentage of just over 26%.

With goals in the 80th minute or later in five consecutive outings, the Lions of Chinguetti have shown a tendency to stay competitive until the final whistle, but they have also struggled early on, conceding first in six of their last eight matches.

Mauritania’s upcoming double-header against Burkina Faso will go a long way in determining their chances of returning to AFCON, having missed out on the most recent edition and ending a run of three consecutive appearances.

Victory on Friday would require the visitors to achieve something they have not managed since June 2023 - win an AFCON qualifier on the road, as their last four away qualifiers have produced just one draw and three defeats.

Mauritania Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Mohamed Ouedraogo is sidelined for Burkina Faso due to injury, but Issa Kabore appears fit to feature despite picking up a knock in his last outing for Wrexham.

In a surprise development, Issoufou Dayo has reversed his international retirement and returned to the Burkina Faso squad.

The centre-back announced his retirement from international football in January following the Africa Cup of Nations, but is now back in contention.

Abderrahmane Sarr and Guessouma Fofana, who last featured for Mauritania in March, have both been recalled by Aritz Lopez Garai.

Aboubakary Koita has recorded two goals and two assists in his last four club matches, and the AEK Athens forward will look to continue his fine form on international duty.

Hinshelwood is known for his versatility but of late he has impressed in the No 10 role. He added: “I'll play anywhere the manager needs or wants me to play, but I'm really enjoying the higher position. I think I can contribute with goals and assists.

“When I first came through, I was playing full-back all the time, and I thought that was going to be me for the rest of my career.
